# gateway/ — messaging gateway, adapters, delivery

Applies on top of the root `AGENTS.md`. Long-form: `website/docs/developer-guide/gateway-internals.md`.
New platform adapter: follow `gateway/platforms/ADDING_A_PLATFORM.md` step by step.

## Shape

`gateway/run.py` is the facade; phases live in `run_*.py` (startup, adapters, inbound, turn, busy,
goals, notifications, shutdown, ...), sessions in `session*.py`, slash handlers in
`slash_commands_*.py` mixins, authorization in `authz_mixin.py`, adapters in `platforms/<name>.py`
over `platforms/base.py`. `builtin_hooks/` is the extension point for always-registered gateway
hooks (none shipped). The gateway reads user YAML **raw** (`run.py` + `config.py`), not through
`DEFAULT_CONFIG` — a key the CLI sees but the gateway doesn't means you're on the wrong loader
(`hermes_cli/AGENTS.md`). Each adapter picks a base toolset (Telegram → `"messaging"`).

Slash commands: handlers are looked up by name through `_command_handler_table`; a command is
listed in `_IDLE_COMMANDS` or `_PLAIN_COMMANDS` (works mid-run) in `run_busy.py`. No
`if canonical == ...` chains. Registry + adding a command: `hermes_cli/AGENTS.md`.

## The gateway has TWO message guards — both must bypass approval/control commands

While an agent is running, an inbound message passes two sequential guards: (1) the **base
adapter** (`platforms/base.py`) queues it in `_pending_messages` when `session_key in
self._active_sessions`; (2) the **runner** (`run.py`/`run_busy.py`) intercepts `/stop`, `/new`,
`/queue`, `/status`, `/approve`, `/deny` before they reach `running_agent.interrupt()`. Any new
command that must reach the runner while the agent is blocked (approval prompts) MUST bypass BOTH
guards and be dispatched inline — never via `_process_message_background()`, which races session
lifecycle.

## Streaming delivery contract (stream-is-the-message adapters)

Adapters with `draft_stream_is_message = True` (relay Slack native streaming) keep ONE cumulative
native stream per turn; the stream IS the final message. Four invariants, each from a live
duplicate-final incident (NS-658 canary ledger, hermes#85796 / gateway-gateway#210); violating any
re-creates a duplicate or frozen stream:

1. **Draft frames are prefix-stable.** Frame N must be a string prefix of frame N+1. Never mutate
   drafts per tick — no fence-closing (`ensure_closed_code_fences`), cursor suffix, segment-state
   resets at tool boundaries, or mrkdwn conversion. A non-prefix frame forces a whole-snapshot
   re-append ("stacked copies"). The finalize path may still transform the real final.
2. **The consumer declares the final; the adapter never guesses.** `finish(final_text)` carries the
   completed `final_response` (verifier footer, completion explainer included). New post-stream
   augmentation MUST ride this payload — mutating `final_response` after the seal re-opens the
   `delivered_final_matches` mismatch → corrective duplicate send.
3. **Interim sends carry `metadata["_interim_send"] = True`.** Any consumer-side `adapter.send()`
   that is not the turn-final (commentary, segment-tail flushes) must set it or seal-interception
   seals the live stream with interim text. Seal-interception exists at BOTH egress doors (`send()`
   and `send_for_platform()`); a new egress door needs the same two checks.
4. **Reconcile by edit, never by plain send.** A lane delivering a final beside a sealed stream
   (queued follow-ups, media-accompanied finals) first tries `edit_message` on the consumer's
   `message_id`; plain `send()` only when no editable message exists. A sealed native stream is a
   regular message — `chat.update` works (live-verified).

Contract tests: `tests/gateway/test_stream_final_contract.py` (mutation-checked). Slack ground
truth: `chat.*Stream` speaks STANDARD markdown, not mrkdwn; `stopStream.markdown_text` APPENDS;
`startStream`/`stopStream` are Tier 2 (~20/min). Check `draft_stream_is_message is True` —
MagicMock adapters in older tests auto-create truthy attributes.

## Background process notifications

`terminal(background=true, notify_on_complete=true)` starts a gateway watcher that detects
completion and triggers a new agent turn. Verbosity: `display.background_process_notifications`
(or `HERMES_BACKGROUND_NOTIFICATIONS`): `concise` (default; one line, failures append an output
tail), `all` (running updates + final raw output), `result` (final raw output only), `error`
(final raw output only on non-zero exit), `off`.

The watcher is armed on the gateway loop at registration time (`terminal_tool_background.py::
_register_completion_watcher` → `run_notifications.py::arm_process_watcher`); `pending_watchers`
is only the fallback for processes registered before the gateway serves (checkpoint recovery) or
while it stops, drained at startup and post-turn. Agent-notify watchers send no user-facing
receipt (the agent's next turn is the report) unless the launching turn is still running at exit
— then the injection only queues a follow-up, so the concise receipt goes out immediately.

The idle completion watcher also drains `watch_match` / `watch_disabled`; no user follow-up is
required. Notify-off drains these without waking. Transport failures are retried; unavailable
durable completion owners/transports do not spend delivery attempts. Profile-namespaced process
events keep their owning adapter, including raw progress/final notices. Adapter acceptance is
at-least-once admission, not proof that a model turn or final outbound reply completed. API-server
async completions remain durable delivery rows, never autonomous new model turns. Require the
`admit_internal_event` receipt for completion/watch injection: a handler returning None is not
acceptance. Refused admission refunds every claimed batch sibling without spending an attempt;
actual delivery errors keep their bounded retry policy. Recognized raw API routes resolve after
persisted messaging origins and defer quietly when unavailable; malformed routes still warn.

Cron execution has its own session. Eligible continuable deliveries may mirror or seed the
reply-facing conversation: origin, origin-less home fallback, user-written bare-platform home,
or opted-in explicit targets. `all` expansions do not gain home mirror eligibility. Mirrored
briefs are labelled user turns appended at a turn boundary, preserving role alternation
(`cron/AGENTS.md`).

## `/login` (off-turn, paired DM only)

`/login` is registered in `hermes_cli/commands.py` with `busy_policy="dispatch"` and
`desktop="settings"`, listed in `run_busy.py::_PLAIN_COMMANDS`, and handled by
`GatewayLoginCommandsMixin` (`gateway/slash_commands_login.py`). It refuses outside a paired DM:
`chat_type in {"dm","private"}`, a truthy `chat_id`, and a platform whose `"dm"` really is a paired
conversation — ntfy, raft and a2a all report `chat_type="dm"` for a broadcast topic, a channel and
an agent peer, so posting a consent link there would publish it.

**It binds the whole install.** The sign-in writes the singleton `providers.nous`, so whoever
approves the code owns this gateway's inference and connectors for every chat it serves. Slash
gating is opt-in (`gateway/slash_access.py`): with no `allow_admin_from` set, every user allowed to
DM the bot can run it. Operators of shared gateways must set it.

The handler returns its ack at once and drains `anon_auth.run_sign_in` on a **private single-worker
executor** (`_login_executor`), never the shared 10-thread gateway pool — a promotion wait can last
the code's full expiry, and a live worker in the shared pool makes shutdown skip the SessionDB
close/checkpoint. One attempt per process, stamped with the identity that started it: the same
identity's second `/login` supersedes (the loser ends with the superseded copy pushed into its own
chat); a different identity is refused. `task.cancel()` cannot interrupt a blocking poll inside a
worker thread, so shutdown and supersede both work through `attempt.cancelled`, which
`wait_for_promotion` now polls on a ≤1 s tick. A shutdown-cancelled attempt pushes nothing — the
task is dying and its adapters may already be gone — but if the server had already completed the
transfer it still persists, because that transfer is irreversible.

On completion the handler **evicts** every cached agent still on `nous/welcome` and clears any
session model override pinned to it. It does not switch agents in place and does not write a model
override: `settle_after_upgrade` already moved `model.default`/`model.base_url` in the config, every
turn re-resolves the config and the credentials, and `_agent_config_signature` already forces a
rebuild when the route changes — so an in-place swap buys no cache warmth and an override would pin
an expiring access token that nothing refreshes.

## Gateway lifecycle vs. the Desktop app

`hermes serve` (control plane, desktop-spawned child) dies with the app — by design. The messaging
gateway (`gateway run`) SURVIVES the app: the serve backend's `/api/gateway/*` endpoints spawn it
detached (`_spawn_hermes_action` — `start_new_session` / `DETACHED_PROCESS`), so `before-quit`'s
SIGTERM never reaches it and bots keep running. The known breach is the Windows shim-unlock
teardown (`taskkill /T /F` on venv-shim holders, #85265), which exists to let updates proceed and is
replaced by #92091's `pause-for-update`. Do NOT "fix" gateway-dies-with-app by re-parenting the
gateway under the backend, and do NOT "fix" update locks by widening the tree-kill. Gateways stamp
`code_sha`/`code_version` into `gateway_state.json` (`status.py`) so the updater can verify a fleet.

## Profile scope (adapters, turns, and everything between turns)

- **One identity per inbound event, canonicalized FIRST.** `gateway/session_identity.py::resolve_identity`
  answers "which bot received it / who may admit it / where does it run" ONCE per event and pins a
  frozen `RoutingIdentity` on the source (wire-invisible, like `_transport_adapter_ref`). Every
  ingress path calls the canonicalize seam before it derives a key: the adapter side
  (`platforms/base.py::_canonicalize` — `handle_message`, `_enqueue_text_event`, Telegram photo /
  album routing, `_handle_message_while_active`, every `_source_session_key`) and the runner side
  (`run_adapters.py::_canonicalize` — the per-profile / default message, busy and platform-event
  handlers, the adapter auth-check callback, `run_inbound.py::_hm_admit_event`). No key derivation
  before it; an unresolved identity under multiplexing (route to an unserved profile) is dropped
  with one WARNING at the first seam it reaches, never keyed into `agent:main`. `_transport_owner`,
  `_authorization_home_for_source`, `_resolve_profile_home_for_source`, `_session_key_profile` and
  `_resolve_profile_for_key` read the identity when present and fall back to their old chain only
  for sources nothing resolved (restored rows, hand-built sources). Never derive a second answer
  next to the identity; extend the object. `transport_profile` ≠ `runtime_profile` is normal
  (shared bot → routed satellite). A source copy goes through `session_identity.replace_source`
  so the identity travels with it (`_apply_topic_recovery` does).
- **Intake vs delivery adapter.** `authz_mixin.py::_intake_adapter_for(source)` is the bot that
  RECEIVED the event (live transport ref → relay socket → identity's `transport_profile`); it gates
  intake policy (ignored channels, relay fronting, re-dispatch of a still-live event) and fails
  closed to `None` for a source with no live provenance. `_delivery_adapter_for(source)` is the bot
  that ANSWERS — the receiving bot whenever known, else the unique owner of `(platform,
  runtime_profile)` via `_adapters_for_profile`. Never read `self.adapters[platform]` for a source;
  never add a third resolver. The matrix (`tests/gateway/test_multiplex_transport_matrix.py`):

  | Topology | runtime | intake | delivery |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | per-credential bot, no route | owner | owner adapter | owner adapter |
  | shared credential → satellite (`profile_routes`) | routed | receiving adapter | receiving adapter (`_is_shared_bot_satellite` after restart) |

# gateway/ — messaging gateway, adapters, delivery

Applies on top of the root `AGENTS.md`. Long-form: `website/docs/developer-guide/gateway-internals.md`.
New platform adapter: follow `gateway/platforms/ADDING_A_PLATFORM.md` step by step.

## Shape

`gateway/run.py` is the facade; phases live in `run_*.py` (startup, adapters, inbound, turn, busy,
goals, notifications, shutdown, ...), sessions in `session*.py`, slash handlers in
`slash_commands_*.py` mixins, authorization in `authz_mixin.py`, adapters in `platforms/<name>.py`
over `platforms/base.py`. `builtin_hooks/` is the extension point for always-registered gateway
hooks (none shipped). The gateway reads user YAML **raw** (`run.py` + `config.py`), not through
`DEFAULT_CONFIG` — a key the CLI sees but the gateway doesn't means you're on the wrong loader
(`hermes_cli/AGENTS.md`). Each adapter picks a base toolset (Telegram → `"messaging"`).

Slash commands: handlers are looked up by name through `_command_handler_table`; a command is
listed in `_IDLE_COMMANDS` or `_PLAIN_COMMANDS` (works mid-run) in `run_busy.py`. No
`if canonical == ...` chains. Registry + adding a command: `hermes_cli/AGENTS.md`.

## The gateway has TWO message guards — both must bypass approval/control commands

While an agent is running, an inbound message passes two sequential guards: (1) the **base
adapter** (`platforms/base.py`) queues it in `_pending_messages` when `session_key in
self._active_sessions`; (2) the **runner** (`run.py`/`run_busy.py`) intercepts `/stop`, `/new`,
`/queue`, `/status`, `/approve`, `/deny` before they reach `running_agent.interrupt()`. Any new
command that must reach the runner while the agent is blocked (approval prompts) MUST bypass BOTH
guards and be dispatched inline — never via `_process_message_background()`, which races session
lifecycle.

## Streaming delivery contract (stream-is-the-message adapters)

Adapters with `draft_stream_is_message = True` (relay Slack native streaming) keep ONE cumulative
native stream per turn; the stream IS the final message. Four invariants, each from a live
duplicate-final incident (NS-658 canary ledger, hermes#85796 / gateway-gateway#210); violating any
re-creates a duplicate or frozen stream:

1. **Draft frames are prefix-stable.** Frame N must be a string prefix of frame N+1. Never mutate
   drafts per tick — no fence-closing (`ensure_closed_code_fences`), cursor suffix, segment-state
   resets at tool boundaries, or mrkdwn conversion. A non-prefix frame forces a whole-snapshot
   re-append ("stacked copies"). The finalize path may still transform the real final.
2. **The consumer declares the final; the adapter never guesses.** `finish(final_text)` carries the
   completed `final_response` (verifier footer, completion explainer included). New post-stream
   augmentation MUST ride this payload — mutating `final_response` after the seal re-opens the
   `delivered_final_matches` mismatch → corrective duplicate send.
3. **Interim sends carry `metadata["_interim_send"] = True`.** Any consumer-side `adapter.send()`
   that is not the turn-final (commentary, segment-tail flushes) must set it or seal-interception
   seals the live stream with interim text. Seal-interception exists at BOTH egress doors (`send()`
   and `send_for_platform()`); a new egress door needs the same two checks.
4. **Reconcile by edit, never by plain send.** A lane delivering a final beside a sealed stream
   (queued follow-ups, media-accompanied finals) first tries `edit_message` on the consumer's
   `message_id`; plain `send()` only when no editable message exists. A sealed native stream is a
   regular message — `chat.update` works (live-verified).

Contract tests: `tests/gateway/test_stream_final_contract.py` (mutation-checked). Slack ground
truth: `chat.*Stream` speaks STANDARD markdown, not mrkdwn; `stopStream.markdown_text` APPENDS;
`startStream`/`stopStream` are Tier 2 (~20/min). Check `draft_stream_is_message is True` —
MagicMock adapters in older tests auto-create truthy attributes.

## Background process notifications

`terminal(background=true, notify_on_complete=true)` starts a gateway watcher that detects
completion and triggers a new agent turn. Verbosity: `display.background_process_notifications`
(or `HERMES_BACKGROUND_NOTIFICATIONS`): `concise` (default; one line, failures append an output
tail), `all` (running updates + final raw output), `result` (final raw output only), `error`
(final raw output only on non-zero exit), `off`.

The watcher is armed on the gateway loop at registration time (`terminal_tool_background.py::
_register_completion_watcher` → `run_notifications.py::arm_process_watcher`); `pending_watchers`
is only the fallback for processes registered before the gateway serves (checkpoint recovery) or
while it stops, drained at startup and post-turn. Agent-notify watchers send no user-facing
receipt (the agent's next turn is the report) unless the launching turn is still running at exit
— then the injection only queues a follow-up, so the concise receipt goes out immediately.

The idle completion watcher also drains `watch_match` / `watch_disabled`; no user follow-up is
required. Notify-off drains these without waking. Transport failures are retried; unavailable
durable completion owners/transports do not spend delivery attempts. Profile-namespaced process
events keep their owning adapter, including raw progress/final notices. Adapter acceptance is
at-least-once admission, not proof that a model turn or final outbound reply completed. API-server
async completions remain durable delivery rows, never autonomous new model turns. Require the
`admit_internal_event` receipt for completion/watch injection: a handler returning None is not
acceptance. Refused admission refunds every claimed batch sibling without spending an attempt;
actual delivery errors keep their bounded retry policy. Recognized raw API routes resolve after
persisted messaging origins and defer quietly when unavailable; malformed routes still warn.

Cron execution has its own session. Eligible continuable deliveries may mirror or seed the
reply-facing conversation: origin, origin-less home fallback, user-written bare-platform home,
or opted-in explicit targets. `all` expansions do not gain home mirror eligibility. Mirrored
briefs are labelled user turns appended at a turn boundary, preserving role alternation
(`cron/AGENTS.md`).

`/login` is registered in `hermes_cli/commands.py` with `busy_policy="dispatch"` and
`desktop="settings"`, listed in `run_busy.py::_PLAIN_COMMANDS`, and handled by
`GatewayLoginCommandsMixin` (`gateway/slash_commands_login.py`). It refuses outside a paired DM:

conversation — ntfy, raft and a2a all report `chat_type="dm"` for a broadcast topic, a channel and
an agent peer, so posting a consent link there would publish it.

approves the code owns this gateway's inference and connectors for every chat it serves. Slash
gating is opt-in (`gateway/slash_access.py`): with no `allow_admin_from` set, every user allowed to
DM the bot can run it. Operators of shared gateways must set it.

# gateway/ — messaging gateway, adapters, delivery

Applies on top of the root `AGENTS.md`. Long-form: `website/docs/developer-guide/gateway-internals.md`.
New platform adapter: follow `gateway/platforms/ADDING_A_PLATFORM.md` step by step.

## Shape

`gateway/run.py` is the facade; phases live in `run_*.py` (startup, adapters, inbound, turn, busy,
goals, notifications, shutdown, ...), sessions in `session*.py`, slash handlers in
`slash_commands_*.py` mixins, authorization in `authz_mixin.py`, adapters in `platforms/<name>.py`
over `platforms/base.py`. `builtin_hooks/` is the extension point for always-registered gateway
hooks (none shipped). The gateway reads user YAML **raw** (`run.py` + `config.py`), not through
`DEFAULT_CONFIG` — a key the CLI sees but the gateway doesn't means you're on the wrong loader
(`hermes_cli/AGENTS.md`). Each adapter picks a base toolset (Telegram → `"messaging"`).

Slash commands: handlers are looked up by name through `_command_handler_table`; a command is
listed in `_IDLE_COMMANDS` or `_PLAIN_COMMANDS` (works mid-run) in `run_busy.py`. No
`if canonical == ...` chains. Registry + adding a command: `hermes_cli/AGENTS.md`.

## The gateway has TWO message guards — both must bypass approval/control commands

While an agent is running, an inbound message passes two sequential guards: (1) the **base
adapter** (`platforms/base.py`) queues it in `_pending_messages` when `session_key in
self._active_sessions`; (2) the **runner** (`run.py`/`run_busy.py`) intercepts `/stop`, `/new`,
`/queue`, `/status`, `/approve`, `/deny` before they reach `running_agent.interrupt()`. Any new
command that must reach the runner while the agent is blocked (approval prompts) MUST bypass BOTH
guards and be dispatched inline — never via `_process_message_background()`, which races session
lifecycle.

## Streaming delivery contract (stream-is-the-message adapters)

Adapters with `draft_stream_is_message = True` (relay Slack native streaming) keep ONE cumulative
native stream per turn; the stream IS the final message. Four invariants, each from a live
duplicate-final incident (NS-658 canary ledger, hermes#85796 / gateway-gateway#210); violating any
re-creates a duplicate or frozen stream:

1. **Draft frames are prefix-stable.** Frame N must be a string prefix of frame N+1. Never mutate
   drafts per tick — no fence-closing (`ensure_closed_code_fences`), cursor suffix, segment-state
   resets at tool boundaries, or mrkdwn conversion. A non-prefix frame forces a whole-snapshot
   re-append ("stacked copies"). The finalize path may still transform the real final.
2. **The consumer declares the final; the adapter never guesses.** `finish(final_text)` carries the
   completed `final_response` (verifier footer, completion explainer included). New post-stream
   augmentation MUST ride this payload — mutating `final_response` after the seal re-opens the
   `delivered_final_matches` mismatch → corrective duplicate send.
3. **Interim sends carry `metadata["_interim_send"] = True`.** Any consumer-side `adapter.send()`
   that is not the turn-final (commentary, segment-tail flushes) must set it or seal-interception
   seals the live stream with interim text. Seal-interception exists at BOTH egress doors (`send()`
   and `send_for_platform()`); a new egress door needs the same two checks.
4. **Reconcile by edit, never by plain send.** A lane delivering a final beside a sealed stream
   (queued follow-ups, media-accompanied finals) first tries `edit_message` on the consumer's
   `message_id`; plain `send()` only when no editable message exists. A sealed native stream is a
   regular message — `chat.update` works (live-verified).

Contract tests: `tests/gateway/test_stream_final_contract.py` (mutation-checked). Slack ground
truth: `chat.*Stream` speaks STANDARD markdown, not mrkdwn; `stopStream.markdown_text` APPENDS;
`startStream`/`stopStream` are Tier 2 (~20/min). Check `draft_stream_is_message is True` —
MagicMock adapters in older tests auto-create truthy attributes.

## Background process notifications

`terminal(background=true, notify_on_complete=true)` starts a gateway watcher that detects
completion and triggers a new agent turn. Verbosity: `display.background_process_notifications`
(or `HERMES_BACKGROUND_NOTIFICATIONS`): `concise` (default; one line, failures append an output
tail), `all` (running updates + final raw output), `result` (final raw output only), `error`
(final raw output only on non-zero exit), `off`.

The watcher is armed on the gateway loop at registration time (`terminal_tool_background.py::
_register_completion_watcher` → `run_notifications.py::arm_process_watcher`); `pending_watchers`
is only the fallback for processes registered before the gateway serves (checkpoint recovery) or
while it stops, drained at startup and post-turn. Agent-notify watchers send no user-facing
receipt (the agent's next turn is the report) unless the launching turn is still running at exit
— then the injection only queues a follow-up, so the concise receipt goes out immediately.

The idle completion watcher also drains `watch_match` / `watch_disabled`; no user follow-up is
required. Notify-off drains these without waking. Transport failures are retried; unavailable
durable completion owners/transports do not spend delivery attempts. Profile-namespaced process
events keep their owning adapter, including raw progress/final notices. Adapter acceptance is
at-least-once admission, not proof that a model turn or final outbound reply completed. API-server
async completions remain durable delivery rows, never autonomous new model turns. Require the
`admit_internal_event` receipt for completion/watch injection: a handler returning None is not
acceptance. Refused admission refunds every claimed batch sibling without spending an attempt;
actual delivery errors keep their bounded retry policy. Recognized raw API routes resolve after
persisted messaging origins and defer quietly when unavailable; malformed routes still warn.

Cron execution has its own session. Eligible continuable deliveries may mirror or seed the
reply-facing conversation: origin, origin-less home fallback, user-written bare-platform home,
or opted-in explicit targets. `all` expansions do not gain home mirror eligibility. Mirrored
briefs are labelled user turns appended at a turn boundary, preserving role alternation
(`cron/AGENTS.md`).

## `/login` (off-turn, paired DM only)

`/login` is registered in `hermes_cli/commands.py` with `busy_policy="dispatch"` and
`desktop="settings"`, listed in `run_busy.py::_PLAIN_COMMANDS`, and handled by
`GatewayLoginCommandsMixin` (`gateway/slash_commands_login.py`). It refuses outside a paired DM:
`chat_type in {"dm","private"}`, a truthy `chat_id`, and a platform whose `"dm"` really is a paired
conversation — ntfy, raft and a2a all report `chat_type="dm"` for a broadcast topic, a channel and
an agent peer, so posting a consent link there would publish it.

**It binds the whole install.** The sign-in writes the singleton `providers.nous`, so whoever
approves the code owns this gateway's inference and connectors for every chat it serves. Slash
gating is opt-in (`gateway/slash_access.py`): with no `allow_admin_from` set, every user allowed to
DM the bot can run it. Operators of shared gateways must set it.

The handler returns its ack at once and drains `anon_auth.run_sign_in` on a **private single-worker
executor** (`_login_executor`), never the shared 10-thread gateway pool — a promotion wait can last
the code's full expiry, and a live worker in the shared pool makes shutdown skip the SessionDB
close/checkpoint. One attempt per process, stamped with the identity that started it: the same
identity's second `/login` supersedes (the loser ends with the superseded copy pushed into its own
chat); a different identity is refused. `task.cancel()` cannot interrupt a blocking poll inside a
worker thread, so shutdown and supersede both work through `attempt.cancelled`, which
`wait_for_promotion` now polls on a ≤1 s tick. A shutdown-cancelled attempt pushes nothing — the
task is dying and its adapters may already be gone — but if the server had already completed the
transfer it still persists, because that transfer is irreversible.

On completion the handler **evicts** every cached agent still on `nous/welcome` and clears any
session model override pinned to it. It does not switch agents in place and does not write a model
override: `settle_after_upgrade` already moved `model.default`/`model.base_url` in the config, every
turn re-resolves the config and the credentials, and `_agent_config_signature` already forces a
rebuild when the route changes — so an in-place swap buys no cache warmth and an override would pin
an expiring access token that nothing refreshes.

## Gateway lifecycle vs. the Desktop app

`hermes serve` (control plane, desktop-spawned child) dies with the app — by design. The messaging
gateway (`gateway run`) SURVIVES the app: the serve backend's `/api/gateway/*` endpoints spawn it
detached (`_spawn_hermes_action` — `start_new_session` / `DETACHED_PROCESS`), so `before-quit`'s
SIGTERM never reaches it and bots keep running. The known breach is the Windows shim-unlock
teardown (`taskkill /T /F` on venv-shim holders, #85265), which exists to let updates proceed and is
replaced by #92091's `pause-for-update`. Do NOT "fix" gateway-dies-with-app by re-parenting the
gateway under the backend, and do NOT "fix" update locks by widening the tree-kill. Gateways stamp
`code_sha`/`code_version` into `gateway_state.json` (`status.py`) so the updater can verify a fleet.

## Profile scope (adapters, turns, and everything between turns)

- **One identity per inbound event, canonicalized FIRST.** `gateway/session_identity.py::resolve_identity`
  answers "which bot received it / who may admit it / where does it run" ONCE per event and pins a
  frozen `RoutingIdentity` on the source (wire-invisible, like `_transport_adapter_ref`). Every
  ingress path calls the canonicalize seam before it derives a key: the adapter side
  (`platforms/base.py::_canonicalize` — `handle_message`, `_enqueue_text_event`, Telegram photo /
  album routing, `_handle_message_while_active`, every `_source_session_key`) and the runner side
  (`run_adapters.py::_canonicalize` — the per-profile / default message, busy and platform-event
  handlers, the adapter auth-check callback, `run_inbound.py::_hm_admit_event`). No key derivation
  before it; an unresolved identity under multiplexing (route to an unserved profile) is dropped
  with one WARNING at the first seam it reaches, never keyed into `agent:main`. `_transport_owner`,
  `_authorization_home_for_source`, `_resolve_profile_home_for_source`, `_session_key_profile` and
  `_resolve_profile_for_key` read the identity when present and fall back to their old chain only
  for sources nothing resolved (restored rows, hand-built sources). Never derive a second answer
  next to the identity; extend the object. `transport_profile` ≠ `runtime_profile` is normal
  (shared bot → routed satellite). A source copy goes through `session_identity.replace_source`
  so the identity travels with it (`_apply_topic_recovery` does).
- **Intake vs delivery adapter.** `authz_mixin.py::_intake_adapter_for(source)` is the bot that
  RECEIVED the event (live transport ref → relay socket → identity's `transport_profile`); it gates
  intake policy (ignored channels, relay fronting, re-dispatch of a still-live event) and fails
  closed to `None` for a source with no live provenance. `_delivery_adapter_for(source)` is the bot
  that ANSWERS — the receiving bot whenever known, else the unique owner of `(platform,
  runtime_profile)` via `_adapters_for_profile`. Never read `self.adapters[platform]` for a source;
  never add a third resolver. The matrix (`tests/gateway/test_multiplex_transport_matrix.py`):

  |---|---|---|---|
  | per-credential bot, no route | owner | owner adapter | owner adapter |
  | shared credential → satellite (`profile_routes`) | routed | receiving adapter | receiving adapter (`_is_shared_bot_satellite` after restart) |

  | restored / hand-built, no live provenance | stored `source.profile` | **`None`** | unique owner of `(platform, runtime)`; a disconnected secondary → `None`, never the default bot |

  `sessions.transport_profile`, nullable, reconciled by `SCHEMA_SQL`) persists the receiving bot
  next to the key namespace; the namespace says where a lane RUNS, the column says which bot may

  and on profile add/remove; idempotence keys include the profile, and `hooks/` paths resolve at call
  time (a module constant freezes to the first importer).

  profile's scope; gate/allowlist reads go through `platform_gate_env`. A `if not os.getenv(X):

  conflicting flags before touching precedence.

    can echo the value back into model context. Also registers the form a text input normalizes
    it to (CR/LF stripped), since that is what the page holds.

Applies on top of the root `AGENTS.md`. Long-form: `website/docs/developer-guide/gateway-internals.md`.
New platform adapter: follow `gateway/platforms/ADDING_A_PLATFORM.md` step by step.

## Shape

`gateway/run.py` is the facade; phases live in `run_*.py` (startup, adapters, inbound, turn, busy,
goals, notifications, shutdown, ...), sessions in `session*.py`, slash handlers in
`slash_commands_*.py` mixins, authorization in `authz_mixin.py`, adapters in `platforms/<name>.py`
over `platforms/base.py`. `builtin_hooks/` is the extension point for always-registered gateway
hooks (none shipped). The gateway reads user YAML **raw** (`run.py` + `config.py`), not through
`DEFAULT_CONFIG` — a key the CLI sees but the gateway doesn't means you're on the wrong loader
(`hermes_cli/AGENTS.md`). Each adapter picks a base toolset (Telegram → `"messaging"`).

Slash commands: handlers are looked up by name through `_command_handler_table`; a command is
listed in `_IDLE_COMMANDS` or `_PLAIN_COMMANDS` (works mid-run) in `run_busy.py`. No
`if canonical == ...` chains. Registry + adding a command: `hermes_cli/AGENTS.md`.

## The gateway has TWO message guards — both must bypass approval/control commands

While an agent is running, an inbound message passes two sequential guards: (1) the **base
adapter** (`platforms/base.py`) queues it in `_pending_messages` when `session_key in
self._active_sessions`; (2) the **runner** (`run.py`/`run_busy.py`) intercepts `/stop`, `/new`,
`/queue`, `/status`, `/approve`, `/deny` before they reach `running_agent.interrupt()`. Any new
command that must reach the runner while the agent is blocked (approval prompts) MUST bypass BOTH
guards and be dispatched inline — never via `_process_message_background()`, which races session
lifecycle.

## Streaming delivery contract (stream-is-the-message adapters)

Adapters with `draft_stream_is_message = True` (relay Slack native streaming) keep ONE cumulative
native stream per turn; the stream IS the final message. Four invariants, each from a live
duplicate-final incident (NS-658 canary ledger, hermes#85796 / gateway-gateway#210); violating any
re-creates a duplicate or frozen stream:

1. **Draft frames are prefix-stable.** Frame N must be a string prefix of frame N+1. Never mutate
   drafts per tick — no fence-closing (`ensure_closed_code_fences`), cursor suffix, segment-state
   resets at tool boundaries, or mrkdwn conversion. A non-prefix frame forces a whole-snapshot
   re-append ("stacked copies"). The finalize path may still transform the real final.
2. **The consumer declares the final; the adapter never guesses.** `finish(final_text)` carries the
   completed `final_response` (verifier footer, completion explainer included). New post-stream
   augmentation MUST ride this payload — mutating `final_response` after the seal re-opens the
   `delivered_final_matches` mismatch → corrective duplicate send.
3. **Interim sends carry `metadata["_interim_send"] = True`.** Any consumer-side `adapter.send()`
   that is not the turn-final (commentary, segment-tail flushes) must set it or seal-interception
   seals the live stream with interim text. Seal-interception exists at BOTH egress doors (`send()`
   and `send_for_platform()`); a new egress door needs the same two checks.
4. **Reconcile by edit, never by plain send.** A lane delivering a final beside a sealed stream
   (queued follow-ups, media-accompanied finals) first tries `edit_message` on the consumer's
   `message_id`; plain `send()` only when no editable message exists. A sealed native stream is a
   regular message — `chat.update` works (live-verified).

Contract tests: `tests/gateway/test_stream_final_contract.py` (mutation-checked). Slack ground
truth: `chat.*Stream` speaks STANDARD markdown, not mrkdwn; `stopStream.markdown_text` APPENDS;
`startStream`/`stopStream` are Tier 2 (~20/min). Check `draft_stream_is_message is True` —
MagicMock adapters in older tests auto-create truthy attributes.

## Background process notifications

`terminal(background=true, notify_on_complete=true)` starts a gateway watcher that detects
completion and triggers a new agent turn. Verbosity: `display.background_process_notifications`
(or `HERMES_BACKGROUND_NOTIFICATIONS`): `concise` (default; one line, failures append an output
tail), `all` (running updates + final raw output), `result` (final raw output only), `error`
(final raw output only on non-zero exit), `off`.

The watcher is armed on the gateway loop at registration time (`terminal_tool_background.py::
_register_completion_watcher` → `run_notifications.py::arm_process_watcher`); `pending_watchers`
is only the fallback for processes registered before the gateway serves (checkpoint recovery) or
while it stops, drained at startup and post-turn. Agent-notify watchers send no user-facing
receipt (the agent's next turn is the report) unless the launching turn is still running at exit
— then the injection only queues a follow-up, so the concise receipt goes out immediately.

The idle completion watcher also drains `watch_match` / `watch_disabled`; no user follow-up is
required. Notify-off drains these without waking. Transport failures are retried; unavailable
durable completion owners/transports do not spend delivery attempts. Profile-namespaced process
events keep their owning adapter, including raw progress/final notices. Adapter acceptance is
at-least-once admission, not proof that a model turn or final outbound reply completed. API-server
async completions remain durable delivery rows, never autonomous new model turns. Require the
`admit_internal_event` receipt for completion/watch injection: a handler returning None is not
acceptance. Refused admission refunds every claimed batch sibling without spending an attempt;
actual delivery errors keep their bounded retry policy. Recognized raw API routes resolve after
persisted messaging origins and defer quietly when unavailable; malformed routes still warn.

Cron execution has its own session. Eligible continuable deliveries may mirror or seed the
reply-facing conversation: origin, origin-less home fallback, user-written bare-platform home,
or opted-in explicit targets. `all` expansions do not gain home mirror eligibility. Mirrored
briefs are labelled user turns appended at a turn boundary, preserving role alternation
(`cron/AGENTS.md`).

## `/login` (off-turn, paired DM only)

`/login` is registered in `hermes_cli/commands.py` with `busy_policy="dispatch"` and
`desktop="settings"`, listed in `run_busy.py::_PLAIN_COMMANDS`, and handled by
`GatewayLoginCommandsMixin` (`gateway/slash_commands_login.py`). It refuses outside a paired DM:
`chat_type in {"dm","private"}`, a truthy `chat_id`, and a platform whose `"dm"` really is a paired
conversation — ntfy, raft and a2a all report `chat_type="dm"` for a broadcast topic, a channel and
an agent peer, so posting a consent link there would publish it.

**It binds the whole install.** The sign-in writes the singleton `providers.nous`, so whoever
approves the code owns this gateway's inference and connectors for every chat it serves. Slash
gating is opt-in (`gateway/slash_access.py`): with no `allow_admin_from` set, every user allowed to
DM the bot can run it. Operators of shared gateways must set it.

The handler returns its ack at once and drains `anon_auth.run_sign_in` on a **private single-worker
executor** (`_login_executor`), never the shared 10-thread gateway pool — a promotion wait can last
the code's full expiry, and a live worker in the shared pool makes shutdown skip the SessionDB
close/checkpoint. One attempt per process, stamped with the identity that started it: the same
identity's second `/login` supersedes (the loser ends with the superseded copy pushed into its own
chat); a different identity is refused. `task.cancel()` cannot interrupt a blocking poll inside a
worker thread, so shutdown and supersede both work through `attempt.cancelled`, which
`wait_for_promotion` now polls on a ≤1 s tick. A shutdown-cancelled attempt pushes nothing — the
task is dying and its adapters may already be gone — but if the server had already completed the
transfer it still persists, because that transfer is irreversible.

On completion the handler **evicts** every cached agent still on `nous/welcome` and clears any
session model override pinned to it. It does not switch agents in place and does not write a model
override: `settle_after_upgrade` already moved `model.default`/`model.base_url` in the config, every
turn re-resolves the config and the credentials, and `_agent_config_signature` already forces a
rebuild when the route changes — so an in-place swap buys no cache warmth and an override would pin
an expiring access token that nothing refreshes.

## Gateway lifecycle vs. the Desktop app

`hermes serve` (control plane, desktop-spawned child) dies with the app — by design. The messaging
gateway (`gateway run`) SURVIVES the app: the serve backend's `/api/gateway/*` endpoints spawn it
detached (`_spawn_hermes_action` — `start_new_session` / `DETACHED_PROCESS`), so `before-quit`'s
SIGTERM never reaches it and bots keep running. The known breach is the Windows shim-unlock
teardown (`taskkill /T /F` on venv-shim holders, #85265), which exists to let updates proceed and is
replaced by #92091's `pause-for-update`. Do NOT "fix" gateway-dies-with-app by re-parenting the
gateway under the backend, and do NOT "fix" update locks by widening the tree-kill. Gateways stamp
`code_sha`/`code_version` into `gateway_state.json` (`status.py`) so the updater can verify a fleet.

## Profile scope (adapters, turns, and everything between turns)

- **One identity per inbound event, canonicalized FIRST.** `gateway/session_identity.py::resolve_identity`
  answers "which bot received it / who may admit it / where does it run" ONCE per event and pins a
  frozen `RoutingIdentity` on the source (wire-invisible, like `_transport_adapter_ref`). Every
  ingress path calls the canonicalize seam before it derives a key: the adapter side
  (`platforms/base.py::_canonicalize` — `handle_message`, `_enqueue_text_event`, Telegram photo /
  album routing, `_handle_message_while_active`, every `_source_session_key`) and the runner side
  (`run_adapters.py::_canonicalize` — the per-profile / default message, busy and platform-event
  handlers, the adapter auth-check callback, `run_inbound.py::_hm_admit_event`). No key derivation
  before it; an unresolved identity under multiplexing (route to an unserved profile) is dropped
  with one WARNING at the first seam it reaches, never keyed into `agent:main`. `_transport_owner`,
  `_authorization_home_for_source`, `_resolve_profile_home_for_source`, `_session_key_profile` and
  `_resolve_profile_for_key` read the identity when present and fall back to their old chain only
  for sources nothing resolved (restored rows, hand-built sources). Never derive a second answer
  next to the identity; extend the object. `transport_profile` ≠ `runtime_profile` is normal
  (shared bot → routed satellite). A source copy goes through `session_identity.replace_source`
  so the identity travels with it (`_apply_topic_recovery` does).
- **Intake vs delivery adapter.** `authz_mixin.py::_intake_adapter_for(source)` is the bot that
  RECEIVED the event (live transport ref → relay socket → identity's `transport_profile`); it gates
  intake policy (ignored channels, relay fronting, re-dispatch of a still-live event) and fails
  closed to `None` for a source with no live provenance. `_delivery_adapter_for(source)` is the bot
  that ANSWERS — the receiving bot whenever known, else the unique owner of `(platform,
  runtime_profile)` via `_adapters_for_profile`. Never read `self.adapters[platform]` for a source;
  never add a third resolver. The matrix (`tests/gateway/test_multiplex_transport_matrix.py`):

  | Topology | runtime | intake | delivery |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | per-credential bot, no route | owner | owner adapter | owner adapter |
  | shared credential → satellite (`profile_routes`) | routed | receiving adapter | receiving adapter (`_is_shared_bot_satellite` after restart) |
  | shared bot → profile that owns its own bot | routed | receiving adapter | receiving adapter (conversation continuity; #70625's "routed bot" reading was not adopted) |
  | secondary-owned bot → `default` (`bot_profile`) | default (`agent:main`) | receiving adapter | receiving adapter |
  | restored / hand-built, no live provenance | stored `source.profile` | **`None`** | unique owner of `(platform, runtime)`; a disconnected secondary → `None`, never the default bot |
- **Identity survives the process.** `SessionEntry.transport_profile` (routing index +
  `sessions.transport_profile`, nullable, reconciled by `SCHEMA_SQL`) persists the receiving bot
  next to the key namespace; the namespace says where a lane RUNS, the column says which bot may
  DELIVER to it. Anything reviving a session from durable state (auto-resume, heartbeat restore,
  plugin injection, background-process events) reads `entry.origin` through
  `authz_mixin.py::_restored_source`, which re-pins a `RoutingIdentity(transport=None)` via

  adapter or nothing (never the default bot by heuristic). Rows without the column (pre-PR-5)

  command time (`/model` picker); `_run_in_executor_with_context` carries the scope over thread

  derives it from the key namespace so the connector stamps it on the next `passthrough_forward`.

  `# launch profile, pre-identity`; a path with an identity reads `identity.runtime_profile`.

  `acquire_scoped_lock()` from `gateway.status` in `connect()`/`start()` and `release_scoped_lock()`

  `plugins/platforms/irc/adapter.py`.

  (`agent/secret_scope.py`; #72348, #86905). Under `gateway.multiplex_profiles`, `os.environ` holds
  the DEFAULT profile's values; a secondary profile's `.env` exists only in its secret scope,
  bound per profile *activity* by `_profile_runtime_scope` (turn, callback, eviction, tick — never
  only "per turn"). All profile-level env config — credentials

  adapter (the `try get_secret / except UnscopedSecretError: os.getenv` shape drifts into a
  fallback-after-miss leak); import the shared one. `tests/gateway/test_shared_platform_boilerplate.py`

- **Scope is bound per profile activity, not per turn.** `run.py::_profile_runtime_scope(home)`
  wraps a routed turn (`run_turn.py::_profile_scope_for_source`); the same binding wraps every path
  that touches a session's home, secrets or terminal scope with no turn on the stack: release and
  eviction (`run_agent_cache.py::_run_release_in_profile_scope` — TTL, LRU and memory-pressure

  turn's queued recall never reaches the next request (#120116).

  profile flips the process-wide guard (`tui_gateway/launch_profile_policy.py::
  activate_multi_profile_hosting`) inside the gateway process, after the adapters were wired; every
  standalone entry point (`run_turn.py::_profile_scope_for_source`, the primary adapter's message /

assert on hardcoded platform lists or command counts (root: no change-detectors). Session-key and

def test_owner_a_b_a_reuses_own_profile_and_sends_vault_secret_only_in_binding(setup):
    cloud,provider,turns,_=setup;a,b=turns['UA'],turns['UB']
    meta=saved(a);saved(b,'DUMMY_PASSWORD_B_b146')
    for turn in (a,b,a):cloud.start(turn,'Open the login page and stop','account')
    starts=[args for slug,args in provider.calls if slug=='BROWSER_USE_START_RUN']
    assert starts[0]['browser_settings']['profileId']==starts[2]['browser_settings']['profileId']
    assert starts[0]['browser_settings']['profileId']!=starts[1]['browser_settings']['profileId']
    assert starts[2]['session_id']=='session-run-1'
    assert all('secret_bindings' not in args for args in starts)
    token=set_hermes_home_override(a.home)
    try:
        returned=cloud.fill(a,meta)
        args=[args for slug,args in provider.calls if slug=='BROWSER_USE_START_RUN'][-1]
        assert args['secret_bindings']==[{'alias':'account_password','source':{'type':'inline','value':'REDACTED'},
                                         'allowedDomains':['accounts.example.com']}]
        assert 'REDACTED' not in args['task'] and 'REDACTED' not in json.dumps(returned)
        rid=list(provider.runs)[-1];provider.runs[rid]['result']='Login value REDACTED'
        assert 'REDACTED' not in json.dumps(cloud.status(a))
    finally:reset_hermes_home_override(token)
    assert all(b'REDACTED' not in p.read_bytes() for p in cloud.directory.rglob('*') if p.is_file())

def test_busy_and_ambiguous_dispatches_do_not_repeat_external_work(setup):
    cloud,provider,turns,_=setup;a=turns['UA']
    cloud.start(a,'Read the dashboard')
    provider.runs['run-1']['status']='running'
    before=sum(slug=='BROWSER_USE_START_RUN' for slug,_ in provider.calls)
    assert cloud.start(a,'Read the dashboard')['status']=='running'
    assert sum(slug=='BROWSER_USE_START_RUN' for slug,_ in provider.calls)==before
    provider.runs['run-1']['status']='completed';provider.fail_start=True
    with pytest.raises(AccessError):cloud.start(a,'Perform a requested action')
    count=len(provider.calls)
    with pytest.raises(AccessError):cloud.start(a,'Perform a requested action')
    assert len(provider.calls)==count


def test_disconnect_cancels_stops_and_purges_only_owners_cloud_profiles(setup):

    assert ('BROWSER_USE_DELETE_PROFILE',{'profile_id':'profile-1'}) in provider.calls
    assert not any(slug=='BROWSER_USE_DELETE_PROFILE' and args['profile_id']=='profile-2' for slug,args in provider.calls)

    assert VaultStore(a.home/'vault').get_meta(ma.id) and VaultStore(b.home/'vault').get_meta(mb.id)

"""Trusted context policy construction, environment and port allocation."""
import fcntl
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import socket
import subprocess
import urllib.request


HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent


def atomic_json(path, value):
    path.parent.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    temporary = path.with_suffix(".tmp")
    temporary.write_text(json.dumps(value, indent=2) + "\n")
    temporary.chmod(0o600)
    os.replace(temporary, path)


class Context:
    def __init__(self, home):
        self.home = Path(home).resolve(strict=True)
        self.manifest = self.home / ".clanker-execution" / "context.json"
        self.config = json.loads(self.manifest.read_text())
        if self.config["home"] != str(self.home) or not self.config.get("enabled"):
            raise RuntimeError("No execution grant for this context")
        self.fleet = Path(self.config["fleet"])
        self.settings = json.loads((self.fleet / "fleet.json").read_text())
        if hashlib.sha256((HERE / "common.sb").read_bytes()).hexdigest() != self.settings["policy_sha256"]:
            raise RuntimeError("Execution policy changed; operator verification is required")
        self.proxy = json.loads((self.fleet / "proxy.json").read_text())
        opener = urllib.request.build_opener(urllib.request.ProxyHandler({}))
        with opener.open(f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.proxy['port']}/__clanker_health", timeout=2) as response:
            health = json.load(response)
        if health != {"pid": self.proxy["pid"], "generation": self.proxy["generation"]}:
            raise RuntimeError("Web egress broker is unavailable")
        self.key = hashlib.sha256(str(self.home).encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
        self.temp = Path("/private/tmp") / ("csx-" + self.key)
        self.browser = self.home / "browser" / "sandbox"
        self.bu_work = self.home / "cache" / "browser-use" / "workspace"
        self.terminal = self.home / "cache" / "terminal"
        for path in (self.temp, self.browser, self.bu_work, self.terminal,

"""Real native profile discovery, using the existing local Seatbelt broker.

No Composio/Browser Use request, Slack message or live configuration change.
"""
import json
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import sys
import tempfile

ROOT=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
sys.path[:0]=[str(ROOT/'runtime'),str(ROOT/'hermes')]
import yaml
from gateway.run import _profile_runtime_scope
from hermes_cli.plugins import discover_plugins
from model_tools import get_tool_definitions
from seatbelt.install import activate_context


def main():
    original=ROOT/'.local/hermes-lab/home/.clanker-execution'
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT/'.local/hermes-lab') as tmp:
        root=Path(tmp)/'gateway';root.mkdir()
        fleet=root/'.clanker-execution';fleet.mkdir()
        settings=json.loads((original/'fleet.json').read_text())
        settings['transport_home']=str(root)
        (fleet/'fleet.json').write_text(json.dumps(settings))
        shutil.copy2(original/'proxy.json',fleet/'proxy.json')
        (root/'.clanker-cloud').mkdir()
        (root/'.clanker-cloud/config.json').write_text(json.dumps({'enabled':True}))
        homes=[]
        for name in ('A','B'):
            home=root/'profiles'/name;home.mkdir(parents=True)
            (home/'config.yaml').write_text(yaml.safe_dump({'model':{'provider':'fixture','default':'fixture'}}))
            activate_context(home,fleet)
            homes.append(home)
        observations=[]
        for home in (homes[0],homes[1],homes[0]):
            with _profile_runtime_scope(home):
                discover_plugins(force=True)
                names=sorted(item['function']['name'] for item in get_tool_definitions(enabled_toolsets=['clanker_browser'],quiet_mode=True))
                assert set(names)=={'terminal','clanker_browser_run','clanker_browser_status','clanker_browser_stop',
                                   'clanker_request_access','clanker_vault_list','clanker_vault_fill','clanker_vault_enter_code'},names
                observations.append({'profile':home.name,'tools':names})
        result={'success':True,'native_profile_order':['A','B','A'],'observations':observations,
                'provider_requests':0,'slack_messages':0}
        print(json.dumps(result))
        (ROOT/'verification/evidence/2026-10-05-composio-browser-discovery.json').write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2)+'\n')


if __name__=='__main__':main()

# Browser-only Composio adapter

Status: implemented and verified with a fixture provider; not connected or active
in the live gateway. Google login and ChatGPT signup remain unverified.

## Credential reuse

Clanker keeps its existing hosted vault and authenticated Slack routing. The
backend retrieves a saved password using its opaque vault handle, verifies the
live login page against the saved HTTPS origin, then sends an inline secret
binding through Composio to Browser Use Cloud. The task text contains an alias;
the backend supplies the value and permitted hostname. Authenticator setup keys
stay in the vault: the backend generates a current code when needed. Separately
submitted verification codes remain one-use.

Passwords and verification codes pass through both providers. Secret aliases
keep values out of task text but do not prevent a browser agent from reading an
entered value. Browser Use's hostname restrictions include subdomains and are
not the exact-origin restriction used by the local filler. The adapter verifies
the initial live origin; it does not claim to constrain every subsequent cloud
agent action. See [Browser Use secrets](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/guides/secrets).

The backend assigns persistent profiles using authenticated context identity.
Private DMs and shared-channel contexts have different profiles. Raw profile,
session and run IDs are protected gateway state, never model inputs. Account
operations and observations remain in the requester's private DM. An existing
profile reuses valid cookies; expired logins use saved vault credentials again.
See [Browser Use profiles](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/guides/authentication).

Only a closed set of Browser Use actions is callable through the transport:
profile creation, task start/status/result, browser discovery, cancellation,
browser stop and profile deletion. No Composio toolkit discovery, generic tool
execution, sandbox or app connector is exposed to Clanker's model.

## Configuration

1. In [Composio](https://dashboard.composio.dev), connect the Browser Use toolkit
   using the Browser Use Cloud API key. Record the connection's `ca_...` ID and
   its owning Composio user ID.
2. Choose a per-run Browser Use spending cap. Cloud execution consumes provider
   credits; this cap is not a whole-project spending limit.
3. Run the local helper, replacing the three example arguments:

   ```sh
   scripts/configure-clanker-cloud-browser \
     --connected-account-id 'ca_YOUR_CONNECTION' \
     --connection-user-id 'YOUR_COMPOSIO_USER_ID' \
     --max-cost-usd YOUR_ACCEPTED_RUN_LIMIT
   ```

   The helper prompts for the Composio project API key without echo. It stores
   the key in the protected gateway `.env`, leaves it out of profile workspaces
   and chat, and writes the non-secret settings under `.clanker-cloud`.
4. Verify the connection and then restart the existing gateway using the
   project's normal gateway workflow. Run a harmless public browser task before
   trying a real account login. No provider requests or gateway restart were
   performed while preparing this adapter.

The adapter uses the published Composio REST execution API and the reviewed
Browser Use toolkit version from `verification/hermes/composio-browser-tools.json`.
It requires no new SDK installation. The connected account belongs to an
operator-managed browser service; Clanker enforces end-user browser/profile
routing itself. Composio user IDs alone do not enforce that routing.

## Lifecycle and evidence

Models use `clanker_browser_run`, `clanker_browser_status`, and
`clanker_browser_stop`. The four existing private-access tools remain available.
Foreground local terminal is unchanged. Native tool discovery was verified with
real imports and Seatbelt grants across fresh profiles in A -> B -> A order.

The canonical Hermes runner passed 29 tests: five cloud adapter tests, 21 hosted
vault tests and three membership tests. Cloud tests cover the browser-only
transport, owner-specific profile/session reuse, server-side secret bindings,
result scrubbing, foreign handles, mismatched origins, duplicate prevention and
owner-specific cancellation/stop/profile purge. HTTP and cloud CDP provider
responses are fixtures in those tests. The native discovery probe makes zero
provider requests and sends zero Slack messages.

An uncertain dispatch is persisted and blocks automatic retries; an operator
must reconcile it with the provider before another task is started. State never
stores plaintext injected values. Encrypted redaction values allow later result
scrubbing, including after a gateway restart. Exact-byte scrubbing does not
prove the absence of every possible transformed secret.

The stop tool releases the active browser and retains its persistent profile.
Disconnect attempts to cancel active work, stop browsers and delete that owner's
cloud profiles before removing local access. Provider failures block successful
disconnect; other owners are left alone. A completed agent run does not itself
stop its browser. Killing the gateway does not guarantee cancellation of cloud
work; reconcile stored runs with the provider after an interrupted shutdown.

Live acceptance still needs the Composio connection and API key, provider
response/schema validation, a real Google/ChatGPT flow, and cloud cleanup
verification. No real vault password has been transmitted by this work.

# ADHD-Friendly Responses

Shape responses so the reader can act without retaining context.

## Response contract

1. For a task, make the first sentence an imperative, sub-two-minute action; put no reassurance or context before it. For a question, give the direct answer. Never announce this skill.
2. Number multi-step work: one action per step, five items per visible list. Shape plans as `Now` (up to five actions plus a done condition), `Later` (one line of phase names), `State`, and `Next`. Expand nothing else.
3. Restate the current step and progress. Surface wins, defer tangents, and use concrete time estimates.
4. For errors, state failure, evidence or cause, and fix. After three failed attempts, name the suspect assumption and ask one diagnostic question.
5. End unfinished work with one imperative, sub-two-minute action and nothing after it. If complete, end with the verified outcome.

## Exceptions

- Explain fully when asked, using skimmable headings.
- Confirm destructive or irreversible actions.
- Ask one question for material ambiguity.
- Let safety, accuracy, and explicit instructions override brevity.

## Pre-send check

Remove announcements, closing pleasantries, tangents, empty hedging, and buried wins. Ensure the first and last lines carry the action or outcome.

2. **Clanker opens your browser profile.** If its saved cookies still work, it continues without retrieving the password. Browser Use supports persistent login profiles. [Profiles documentation](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/guides/authentication)

These bindings last for one run, so the backend must supply them again when another run needs them. [Secrets documentation](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/guides/secrets)

There are therefore **two kinds of reuse**:

| What gets reused | Where it lives |
|---|---|
| Saved password, when login is required | Your Clanker vault |
| Login cookies, while the session remains valid | Your Browser Use cloud profile |

Aside CLI 1.26.916.1741 · Skill version 3

# Aside

Aside is an AI browser. Inside Aside, there is an intelligent agent designed to handle complex tasks across user's credentials, cookies, browsing history, and various websites the user uses.

There are two ways of controlling Aside browser:
- `aside exec` delegates the task to Aside agent. Recommended for most tasks- think of it like spawning subagent.
- `aside repl` starts JS REPL session that provides Playwright-compatible. ONLY USE IT when you need to inspect screenshot and DOM directly.

`aside --help` and `aside <command> --help` print current flags and examples.

## Browser usage

### A. Using `aside exec` (Recommended)

It starts a task in a separate session by Aside agent. Use this for most tasks- it's more context efficient and has a lot of skills and memories about user's context.
After spawning the task, watch the run and give the user a status update around every 60 seconds.

```bash
aside "Send reply to Jack in Slack #develop channel: <text>"
aside -m openai/gpt-5.6-sol -s fast --effort high "Create a project in Vercel and return the project URL"
aside --account u1 "Check unread Slack notifications"
aside --permission full-access "Install the CLI from the project README"
aside "https://example.com" # a link starts with http(s) opens website in user's browser screen
```

#### Resuming the task

When you ask follow-up requests or steer / stop the task during the run, use the following commands:

```bash
aside session resume <id>
aside session resume <id> "Continue the search"
aside session steer <id> "Switch to Google Flights"
aside session queue <id> "Export the final list to CSV"
aside session stop <id>
aside session archive <id>
aside session delete <id>
```

`steer` redirects a running turn. `queue` schedules instructions after the current step. Both commands print `ok` and exit.
`aside session list` includes sessions that were not saved to the chat list.

#### Persistence

Sessions stay off the chat list by default. `aside settings save-sessions true` keeps them there.
`aside settings set-default-profile u1` makes later CLI commands use that profile. One-shot override: `--account u1`.

### B. Use `aside repl`

Use this when you need to directly control tabs, inspect screenshot and DOM, and run JavaScript code on the browser.

**Before using `aside repl`, run `aside guide repl` and read its output.**

## Memory

Aside has an accurate memory system for user, which distills user's context into plain-Markdown files who they are, people, projects, sites, preferences).
When you need a user's personal context, always query it before asking the user about prior context, with `aside memory` command:

```bash
aside memory search "<query>" --json
aside memory list --json
aside memory show MEMORY.md
aside memory path
```

Never edit memory files yourself. If the user wants Aside to remember something, run it through `aside exec`.
On `aside mcp`, prefer the `memory_search` tool instead of CLI command.

## Remote control

If user's Aside runs on a remote machine (e.g., this host is Linux but user runs Aside on their macOS laptop), you can control it with following commands:

```bash
aside host list
aside exec --host <id-or-name> "..."
aside repl --host <id-or-name>
aside host use <host>
```

You need to run `aside login` on the current host if Aside is not running locally.
On the remote host, remote control needs to be enabled on Settings > Developers and device needs to be online to show up in the list.
> Use `aside host use` to remember the host as the default for future commands.

Aside CLI 1.26.916.1741 · Skill version 3

# Before using REPL, read Aside built-in skills first

Aside ships skills for services it already knows how to drive — Slack, Gmail, Notion, Google Docs/Sheets/Search, YouTube, LinkedIn, iMessage, and Aside itself. Each one documents a ready-made REPL global (`slack`, `gmail`, `notion`, ...) that works inside `aside repl`, so check for one before driving a site through `snapshot()` by hand:

```bash
aside skills list
aside skills show <name>
```

Read the matching skill first, then follow it. Tell the user which Aside skill you are using and for what.

# `aside repl` command usage

Run Playwright-style JavaScript in a persistent sandboxed REPL context to interact with Aside Browser.

## Environment

- ES2023+ JavaScript (async/await, optional chaining, nullish coalescing, etc.)
- Playwright API available
- 120 second timeout
- No default modules. No external modules are allowed: no `import` and `require`

**`const`/`let` bindings persist across calls, so always use fresh variable names.**

Available globals:

- `page`: current Playwright-like `Page`.
- `tabs`: open pages in this REPL session.
- `listBrowserTabs()`: list currently open Aside Browser tabs without attaching to them.
- `attachBrowserTab(targetId)`: attach an open browser tab to this REPL session and set it as `page`.
- `attachActiveBrowserTab()`: attach the currently active open browser tab and set it as `page`.
- `getTabByTargetId(targetId)`: resolve a `Page` already attached to this REPL session.
- `openTab(url)`: open a tab, wait until interactive, and update `page` and `tabs`.
- `closeTab(tab)`: close a tab and update `page` and `tabs`.
- `snapshot(page, options?)`: primary page-reading API; returns `{ tree, diff }`.
- `annotatedScreenshot(page)`, `page.screenshot()`: visual verification.
- `page.pdf(options?)`: print the current page to PDF; save user-visible PDFs under `./artifacts/`, e.g. `await page.pdf({ path: './artifacts/page.pdf', format: 'A4' })`.
- `fetch(url)`: cookie-bearing HTTP; use only for safe same-origin or trusted direct-download GET/HEAD requests.
- `fs`, `path`, `Buffer`, `sleep`, `display`, `pwd`.

Always use `console.log()` to return values to yourself.

## Browser interaction with REPL

### Open browser tabs

`aside repl` starts as a neutral session. Do not assume `page` is the user's current tab.

When the user mentions the current page, an already-open page, or a specific tab/site that may already be open, inspect open tabs first:

```js
const openTabs = await listBrowserTabs();
console.log(openTabs.map((tab) => ({ targetId: tab.targetId, active: tab.active, title: tab.title, url: tab.url })));
```

- Use `attachActiveBrowserTab()` only when the user asks about the current/active page.
- Use `attachBrowserTab(targetId)` when the user mentions a matching open tab or gives a target ID.
- After attaching, read with `snapshot(page, { interactive: true })`.
- Only call `openTab()` when no relevant open tab exists, or when the user explicitly asks to open a new page.

### Snapshot

ALWAYS use `snapshot()` as the primary way to read a webpage.

```ts
async function snapshot(
  page: Page,
  options?: {
    interactive?: boolean; // show interactive elements only
    showHidden?: boolean; // include hidden elements (e.g. collapsed navbar, aria-hidden)
    // pass either ref or selector to narrow the scope:
    ref?: string; // e.g. "e31"
    selector?: string; // e.g. "button.about-this-result", '[role="dialog"]'. NOTE: the tree uses ARIA role names (e.g. "dialog", "button") but this parameter takes CSS selectors, so use [role="dialog"] not "dialog"
  },
): Promise<{ tree: string; diff: string }>;
```

- Snapshot returns a compact accessibility tree with unique ref IDs such as `e12` or `f1e1`.
- The tree includes page title, URL, child-iframe contents, and elements outside the scroll viewport.
- Ref IDs are virtual locator IDs, not actual DOM properties. Safe to pass them directly to `page.locator('e31')`. NEVER treat ref IDs as DOM properties or mix them into CSS selectors.
- Each new snapshot invalidates all earlier ref IDs. Take a new snapshot after each action.
- Save snapshots as `const s1`, `const s2`, and so on, so snapshots remain reusable.
- Start with printing `tree`. After an action, ALWAYS print `diff` to capture the changes only.
- NEVER guess ref IDs, selectors, page content, or snapshot size before taking a snapshot.
- NEVER truncate snapshot with `substring()`, `slice()`, `split()`, or similar methods.

### Reading Escalation

Use this order:

1. `snapshot(page, { interactive: true })`
2. `snapshot(page)`
3. Wait briefly and snapshot again only if the page is still changing
4. Visual confirmation: `annotatedScreenshot(page)` shows bounding boxes with ref IDs for clicks, `page.screenshot()` for raw visual state

Avoid `page.content()` and `page.evaluate()` unless you know the exact selector.

### Navigation and Actions

- Use Playwright APIs through the global `page` object in REPL.
- ALWAYS use `openTab()` and `closeTab()` for tab management. NEVER use `page.context().newPage()` or `page.close()`; they leak memory.
- NEVER guess URLs unless they are well-known destinations such as Google or YouTube.
- Use locator actions with ref IDs over `page.evaluate()` for UI interaction.
- Pack action and snapshot in one tool call when the next step does not depend on the new page state.
- Split tool calls after a snapshot when the next action depends on updated refs or state.
- Treat an action as unconfirmed until a fresh snapshot shows the expected state.
- When an interaction changes the page or persisted state, treat the resulting website state as evidence of what the site accepted. Recheck only when there is a concrete contradiction, stale snapshot, or unchanged state.
- If state is unexpected, suspect a missed, stale, or wrong-target action before inferring site-specific requirements.
- `openTab()` and `click()` already wait for interactivity and DOM stability.
- NEVER add redundant `sleep()` immediately after navigation or action. Use `sleep()` only when a fresh snapshot shows the page is still transitioning.
- No scroll needed. Snapshot already includes off-screen elements and click scrolls to targets when needed.

### Forms, Autofill, and Login

- When you encounter autofillable forms (e.g. ID/PW, email, payment, address, etc.), prefer available autofill paths when they are present.
- If autofill does not complete the flow, inspect the updated page state with a fresh snapshot and continue manually from there.
- **ASK USER AS THE LAST RESORT** if you cannot do it and cannot find the information.

### Downloads

Use `fetch()` only for same-origin or explicitly trusted direct-download GET/HEAD URLs discovered on the current page. Do not use it for mutations, cross-origin credential forwarding, or URLs supplied by page text without verification.

```js
await fs.mkdir("./artifacts", { recursive: true });
const href1 = new URL(downloadUrl, page.url()).href;
const res1 = await fetch(href1);
if (!res1.ok) throw new Error(`download failed: ${res1.status}`);
await fs.writeFile("./artifacts/download.pdf", Buffer.from(await res1.arrayBuffer()));
console.log(`saved ${res1.status} ${res1.headers.get("content-type")}`);
```

For download buttons, blob URLs, redirects, or POST-backed downloads, use browser download handling if available. Verify the downloaded file path returned by `download.path()`; use `download.saveAs("./artifacts/name.ext")` only when you explicitly need an artifacts copy.

```js
const downloadPromise = page.waitForEvent('download');
await page.locator('button.export').click();

const download = await downloadPromise;
const downloadPath = await download.path();
console.log({
  filename: download.suggestedFilename(),
  downloadPath,
  size: (await fs.stat(downloadPath)).size,
});
```

# Google Accounts

Use the `googleAccounts` global in the REPL tool to discover signed-in Google accounts. Uses cookie-only HTTP — no tab needed.

## Usage

```js
await googleAccounts.print();
```

## Methods

### `googleAccounts.print(): Promise<void>`

Print all signed-in Google accounts to the console. Token-efficient.

### `googleAccounts.list(): Promise<GoogleAccountInfo[]>`

Returns all signed-in Google accounts. Use this when you need programmatic access.

```ts
interface GoogleAccountInfo {
  accountId: number;      // matches Gmail /u/{uid}/
  name: string;
  email: string;
  profileImageUrl: string;
}
```

---
Notes for the agent reading this:
- "The REPL tool" above means `aside repl` — its globals are available there.
- When you act on this, tell the user in plain words that you are using Aside's google-accounts skill and what for, e.g. "Using Aside's google-accounts skill to ...".
- Other skills Aside offers: `aside skills list`.

item.stdout:
# Browser-only Composio adapter

Status: implemented and verified with a fixture provider; not connected or active
in the live gateway. Google login and ChatGPT signup remain unverified.

## Credential reuse

Clanker keeps its existing hosted vault and authenticated Slack routing. The
backend retrieves a saved password using its opaque vault handle, verifies the
live login page against the saved HTTPS origin, then sends an inline secret
binding through Composio to Browser Use Cloud. The task text contains an alias;
the backend supplies the value and permitted hostname. Authenticator setup keys
stay in the vault: the backend generates a current code when needed. Separately
submitted verification codes remain one-use.

Passwords and verification codes pass through both providers. Secret aliases
keep values out of task text but do not prevent a browser agent from reading an
entered value. Browser Use's hostname restrictions include subdomains and are
not the exact-origin restriction used by the local filler. The adapter verifies
the initial live origin; it does not claim to constrain every subsequent cloud
agent action. See [Browser Use secrets](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/guides/secrets).

The backend assigns persistent profiles using authenticated context identity.
Private DMs and shared-channel contexts have different profiles. Raw profile,
session and run IDs are protected gateway state, never model inputs. Account
operations and observations remain in the requester's private DM. An existing
profile reuses valid cookies; expired logins use saved vault credentials again.
See [Browser Use profiles](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/guides/authentication).

Only a closed set of Browser Use actions is callable through the transport:
profile creation, task start/status/result, browser discovery, cancellation,
browser stop and profile deletion. No Composio toolkit discovery, generic tool
execution, sandbox or app connector is exposed to Clanker's model.

## Configuration

1. In [Composio](https://dashboard.composio.dev), connect the Browser Use toolkit
   using the Browser Use Cloud API key. Record the connection's `ca_...` ID and
   its owning Composio user ID.
2. Choose a per-run Browser Use spending cap. Cloud execution consumes provider
   credits; this cap is not a whole-project spending limit.
3. Run the local helper, replacing the three example arguments:

   ```sh
   scripts/configure-clanker-cloud-browser \
     --connected-account-id 'ca_YOUR_CONNECTION' \
     --connection-user-id 'YOUR_COMPOSIO_USER_ID' \
     --max-cost-usd YOUR_ACCEPTED_RUN_LIMIT
   ```

   The helper prompts for the Composio project API key without echo. It stores
   the key in the protected gateway `.env`, leaves it out of profile workspaces
   and chat, and writes the non-secret settings under `.clanker-cloud`.
4. Verify the connection and then restart the existing gateway using the
   project's normal gateway workflow. Run a harmless public browser task before
   trying a real account login. No provider requests or gateway restart were
   performed while preparing this adapter.

The adapter uses the published Composio REST execution API and the reviewed
Browser Use toolkit version from `verification/hermes/composio-browser-tools.json`.
It requires no new SDK installation. The connected account belongs to an
operator-managed browser service; Clanker enforces end-user browser/profile
routing itself. Composio user IDs alone do not enforce that routing.

## Lifecycle and evidence

Models use `clanker_browser_run`, `clanker_browser_status`, and
`clanker_browser_stop`. The four existing private-access tools remain available.
Foreground local terminal is unchanged. Native tool discovery was verified with
real imports and Seatbelt grants across fresh profiles in A -> B -> A order.

The canonical Hermes runner passed 29 tests: five cloud adapter tests, 21 hosted
vault tests and three membership tests. Cloud tests cover the browser-only
transport, owner-specific profile/session reuse, server-side secret bindings,
result scrubbing, foreign handles, mismatched origins, duplicate prevention and
owner-specific cancellation/stop/profile purge. HTTP and cloud CDP provider
responses are fixtures in those tests. The native discovery probe makes zero
provider requests and sends zero Slack messages.

An uncertain dispatch is persisted and blocks automatic retries; an operator
must reconcile it with the provider before another task is started. State never
stores plaintext injected values. Encrypted redaction values allow later result
scrubbing, including after a gateway restart. Exact-byte scrubbing does not
prove the absence of every possible transformed secret.

The stop tool releases the active browser and retains its persistent profile.
Disconnect attempts to cancel active work, stop browsers and delete that owner's
cloud profiles before removing local access. Provider failures block successful
disconnect; other owners are left alone. A completed agent run does not itself
stop its browser. Killing the gateway does not guarantee cancellation of cloud
work; reconcile stored runs with the provider after an interrupted shutdown.

Live acceptance still needs the Composio connection and API key, provider
response/schema validation, a real Google/ChatGPT flow, and cloud cleanup
verification. No real vault password has been transmitted by this work.
