Connect AI agents to external tools. search, execute, link, proxy, and run let you
take actions across 1000+ apps directly; if you can describe it, it is probably supported.
Try execute sooner than you'd think — it validates inputs, checks connections, and tells
you what to fix.

Use dev when you are building an agent with Composio's SDK and want scaffolding,
playground execution, logs, and developer-scoped management commands.

USAGE
  composio <command> [options]
  composio --help [simple|default|full]

MODE
  default help

CORE COMMANDS
  search
    Find tools by use case across all toolkits/apps.
    Usage: composio search <query...> [--toolkits text] [--limit integer] [--human]
      <query...>          One or more semantic use-case queries (e.g. "send emails" "github issues")
      --toolkits          Filter by toolkit slugs, comma-separated
      --limit             Maximum number of results (1-1000)
      --human             Show formatted output instead of default JSON

  execute
    Execute a tool. Validates inputs and connections automatically; use it aggressively.
    Usage: composio execute <slug> [-d, --data text] [--account selector] [--file path] [--dry-run] [--get-schema] | execute -p <slug> -d <text> <slug> -d <text> ...
      <slug>              Tool slug (e.g. "GITHUB_CREATE_ISSUE")
      -d, --data          JSON or JS-style object arguments, e.g. -d '{ repo: "foo" }', @file, or - for stdin
      -p, --parallel      Execute repeated <slug> -d <text> pairs concurrently
      --account           Select a connected account by alias, word_id, or account ID
      --file              Inject a local file path into the single file_uploadable input
      --dry-run           Validate and preview the tool call without executing it
      --get-schema        Fetch and print the CLI-facing input schema

  link
    Connect your account for a toolkit/app.
    Usage: composio link [<toolkit>] [--alias text]
      <toolkit>           Toolkit slug to link (e.g. "github", "gmail")
      --alias             Alias for this connected account

  run
    Run inline TS/JS code with shimmed CLI commands; injected execute(), search(), proxy(), experimental_subAgent(), and z (zod).
    Usage: composio run <code> [-- ...args] | run [-f, --file text] [-- ...args] [--dry-run]
      <code>              Inline Bun ESNext code to evaluate
      -f, --file          Run a TS/JS file instead of inline code
      --dry-run           Preview execute() calls without running remote actions

  proxy
    curl-like access to any toolkit API through Composio using your connected account.
    Usage: composio proxy <url> --toolkit text [--account selector] [-X method] [-H header]... [-d data]
      <url>               Full API endpoint URL
      --toolkit           Toolkit slug whose connected account should be used
      --account           Connected account alias, word_id, or account ID
      -X, --method        HTTP method (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH)
      -H, --header        Header in "Name: value" format. Repeat for multiple.
      -d, --data          Request body as raw text, JSON, @file, or - for stdin

  Typical flow: search → execute (link and tools when needed)

TOOLS
  composio tools info <slug>        Print tool summary and cache its schema
  composio tools list <toolkit>     List tools available in a toolkit
  composio triggers info <slug>     Print trigger type details and schema summaries
  composio triggers list <toolkit>  List available trigger types in a toolkit
  composio artifacts cwd            Print the cwd-scoped session artifact directory


EXAMPLES
  # Find tools — supports multiple queries at once
  composio search "send an email" "create github issue"
  composio search "list calendar events" --toolkits google_calendar --limit 5

  # Connect your account for a toolkit
  composio link github

  # Execute a tool
  composio execute GITHUB_CREATE_ISSUE -d '{ owner: "acme", repo: "app", title: "Bug" }'

  # Execute multiple tools in parallel
  composio execute -p GMAIL_SEND_EMAIL -d '{ recipient_email: "a@b.com", subject: "Hi" }' \
                     SLACK_SEND_MESSAGE -d '{ channel: "general", markdown_text: "Hello" }'

  # Call an API directly through proxy
  composio proxy https://gmail.googleapis.com/gmail/v1/users/me/profile --toolkit gmail

  # Run a script with injected helpers
  composio run 'const me = await execute("GITHUB_GET_THE_AUTHENTICATED_USER"); console.log(me)'

  # Manually install the composio skill when auto-install fails
  composio --install-skill claude
  composio --install-skill composio-cli codex

  # Run a multi-step script with Promise.all
  composio run '
    const [emails, issues] = await Promise.all([
      execute("GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS", { max_results: 5 }),
      execute("GITHUB_LIST_REPOSITORY_ISSUES", { owner: "acme", repo: "app", state: "open" }),
    ]);
    const brief = await experimental_subAgent(`Summarize:\n${emails.prompt()}\n${issues.prompt()}`);
    console.log(brief);
  '

DEVELOPER COMMANDS
  dev       Developer workflows and management: init, logs, projects, toolkits, accounts, and triggers.
  generate  Generate type stubs for toolkits, tools, and triggers (TypeScript | Python).

ACCOUNT
  setup    Install or uninstall agent plugins
  login    Log in to Composio
  logout   Log out from Composio
  whoami   Show current account info
  orgs     Manage default global organization/project context.
  version  Display CLI version
  upgrade  Upgrade CLI to the latest version
  config   View and manage CLI configuration

FILES  (composio files --help)
  ~/.composio/
    CLI configuration and cache directory. Contains your auth state
    (user_data.json), runtime settings (config.json), cached tool definitions
    (tools.json, toolkits.json),
    trigger types, and per-org consumer caches. These caches speed up
    repeated commands — safe to delete, they will be re-fetched on next use.

  /tmp/composio/
    Session artifacts directory. Each CLI session gets a unique subdirectory
    scoped to your working directory. Stores session history and files
    created during run and execute commands (e.g. downloaded attachments,
    generated outputs). Use `composio artifacts cwd` to print the path for
    the current directory's session.

FLAGS
  -h, --help [mode]  Show help for command (simple, default, full)
  --version      Show composio version
  --install-skill [skill-name] <claude|codex|openclaw>
                  Manually install the composio skill for a supported agent

LEARN MORE
  Use `composio <command> --help` for more information about a command.
  Documentation: https://docs.composio.dev

"""Small scoped tools wrapping Hermes's native vault and browser fill path."""
import json
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

from .service import binding
from .store import AccessError

TOOLS = ['clanker_request_access','clanker_vault_list','clanker_vault_fill','clanker_vault_enter_code']


def execute(name,args,**kwargs):
    try:
        turn = binding(kwargs.get('task_id'))
        service = turn.service
        if name=='clanker_request_access':
            return json.dumps(service.call(service.request_access(turn,**args)))
        try:home = service.assert_private(turn)
        except AccessError:
            return json.dumps(service.call(service.move_private(turn)))
        from agent.vault_store import VaultStore
        from tools import browser_vault_tool as native
        with service.lock_for(home):
            store = VaultStore(home/'vault')
            if name=='clanker_vault_list':
                return json.dumps({'items':[meta.to_dict() for meta in sorted(store.list_items(),key=lambda item:item.created_at,reverse=True)]})
            meta = store.get_meta(args['handle'])
            if meta is None:
                raise AccessError('This account is not in your private vault.',403)
            if service.cloud_browser is not None:
                cloud=service.cloud_browser
                if name=='clanker_vault_fill':
                    return json.dumps(cloud.fill(turn,meta))
                if name=='clanker_vault_enter_code':
                    from agent.vault_store import totp_now
                    cloud.login_origin(turn,meta.origin,otp=True)
                    secret=store.resolve_secret(meta.id)
                    code=totp_now(secret['otp_secret']) if secret.get('otp_secret') else service.store.consume_code(
                        team=turn.source.scope_id,owner=turn.source.user_id,home=home,
                        task_id=turn.task_id,handle=meta.id,origin=meta.origin)
                    if not code:
                        return json.dumps(service.call(service.request_code(turn,meta)))
                    return json.dumps(cloud.fill(turn,meta,code=code))
            from seatbelt.context import Context
            supervisor = native._ensure_supervisor(turn.task_id)
            if supervisor is None:
                raise AccessError('Start this task\'s private browser before filling the login.',409)
            Context(home).owned_cdp(supervisor.cdp_url)
            if name=='clanker_vault_fill':
                return native.browser_vault_fill(meta.id,task_id=turn.task_id)
            if name=='clanker_vault_enter_code':
                # Stock OTP generation lacks a handle-to-current-origin check;
                # apply the same exact-origin authorization as password filling.
                native._focus_bound_origin(turn.task_id,str(meta.origin),'otp')
                if native._current_page_origin(turn.task_id)!=meta.origin:
                    raise AccessError('The verification page does not match this saved account.',403)
                code=service.store.consume_code(team=turn.source.scope_id,owner=turn.source.user_id,home=home,
                    task_id=turn.task_id,handle=meta.id,origin=meta.origin)
                result=native.browser_vault_enter_code(meta.id,task_id=turn.task_id,
                    expected_origin=meta.origin,provided_code=code)
                del code
                if json.loads(result).get('error_type')=='prompt_unavailable':
                    return json.dumps(service.call(service.request_code(turn,meta)))
                return result
        raise AccessError('This credential operation is unavailable.')
    except AccessError as error:
        return json.dumps({'success':False,'error':str(error),'status':error.status})
    except Exception:
        return json.dumps({'success':False,'error':'The credential operation could not complete. No secret has been returned.'})


def register_tools(ctx):
    definitions = {
        'clanker_request_access':(
            'Request a private hosted login form for the current HTTPS login page. Call when saved access is missing or expired. In a shared channel, this moves the task to the requester\'s DM. Never ask the user to sign into an inaccessible browser or paste credentials in chat. The secure link is sent by the trusted handler; saving resumes the task automatically.',
            {'label':{'type':'string','description':'Account label, for example Google login. The form is bound to the actual page origin.'},'identifier':{'type':'string','description':'Known email or username, for prefilling the form. Never a password.'}},[]),
        'clanker_vault_list':('List this requester\'s private saved-login handles and metadata. Available only in a private DM. Passwords and setup keys are never returned.',{},[]),
        'clanker_vault_fill':('Fill the saved password directly into this task\'s supervised browser on its exact permitted origin. Type the metadata username yourself first. No secret is returned.',{'handle':{'type':'string'}},['handle']),
        'clanker_vault_enter_code':('Enter an authenticator or current verification code on the saved login origin. Without a setup key, send a private hosted one-time-code form and resume automatically after submission. No code or setup key is returned.',{'handle':{'type':'string'}},['handle']),
    }
    for name,(description,properties,required) in definitions.items():
        schema={'name':name,'description':description,'parameters':{'type':'object','properties':properties,'required':required,'additionalProperties':False}}
        ctx.register_tool(name,'clanker_browser',schema,lambda args,_name=name,**kwargs:execute(_name,args,**kwargs),description=description,emoji='🔐')

import json
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

from .service import binding
from .store import AccessError

TOOLS = ['clanker_request_access','clanker_vault_list','clanker_vault_fill','clanker_vault_enter_code']


def execute(name,args,**kwargs):
    try:
        turn = binding(kwargs.get('task_id'))
        service = turn.service
        if name=='clanker_request_access':
            return json.dumps(service.call(service.request_access(turn,**args)))
        try:home = service.assert_private(turn)
        except AccessError:
            return json.dumps(service.call(service.move_private(turn)))
        from agent.vault_store import VaultStore
        from tools import browser_vault_tool as native
        with service.lock_for(home):
            store = VaultStore(home/'vault')
            if name=='clanker_vault_list':
                return json.dumps({'items':[meta.to_dict() for meta in sorted(store.list_items(),key=lambda item:item.created_at,reverse=True)]})
            meta = store.get_meta(args['handle'])
            if meta is None:
                raise AccessError('This account is not in your private vault.',403)
            if service.cloud_browser is not None:
                cloud=service.cloud_browser
                if name=='clanker_vault_fill':
                    return json.dumps(cloud.fill(turn,meta))
                if name=='clanker_vault_enter_code':
                    from agent.vault_store import totp_now
                    cloud.login_origin(turn,meta.origin,otp=True)
                    secret=store.resolve_secret(meta.id)
                    code=totp_now(secret['otp_secret']) if secret.get('otp_secret') else service.store.consume_code(
                        team=turn.source.scope_id,owner=turn.source.user_id,home=home,
                        task_id=turn.task_id,handle=meta.id,origin=meta.origin)
                    if not code:
                        return json.dumps(service.call(service.request_code(turn,meta)))
                    return json.dumps(cloud.fill(turn,meta,code=code))

            supervisor = native._ensure_supervisor(turn.task_id)
            if supervisor is None:
                raise AccessError('Start this task\'s private browser before filling the login.',409)
            Context(home).owned_cdp(supervisor.cdp_url)
            if name=='clanker_vault_fill':
                return native.browser_vault_fill(meta.id,task_id=turn.task_id)
            if name=='clanker_vault_enter_code':
                # Stock OTP generation lacks a handle-to-current-origin check;

                native._focus_bound_origin(turn.task_id,str(meta.origin),'otp')
                if native._current_page_origin(turn.task_id)!=meta.origin:
                    raise AccessError('The verification page does not match this saved account.',403)
                code=service.store.consume_code(team=turn.source.scope_id,owner=turn.source.user_id,home=home,
                    task_id=turn.task_id,handle=meta.id,origin=meta.origin)
                result=native.browser_vault_enter_code(meta.id,task_id=turn.task_id,
                    expected_origin=meta.origin,provided_code=code)
                del code
                if json.loads(result).get('error_type')=='prompt_unavailable':
                    return json.dumps(service.call(service.request_code(turn,meta)))
                return result
        raise AccessError('This credential operation is unavailable.')
    except AccessError as error:
        return json.dumps({'success':False,'error':str(error),'status':error.status})
    except Exception:
        return json.dumps({'success':False,'error':'The credential operation could not complete. No secret has been returned.'})

Never ask the user to sign into an inaccessible browser or paste credentials in chat. The secure link is sent by the trusted handler; saving resumes the task automatically.',

"""Small scoped tools wrapping Hermes's native vault and browser fill path."""
import json
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

from .service import binding
from .store import AccessError

TOOLS = ['clanker_request_access','clanker_vault_list','clanker_vault_fill','clanker_vault_enter_code']


def execute(name,args,**kwargs):
    try:
        turn = binding(kwargs.get('task_id'))
        service = turn.service
        if name=='clanker_request_access':
            return json.dumps(service.call(service.request_access(turn,**args)))
        try:home = service.assert_private(turn)
        except AccessError:
            return json.dumps(service.call(service.move_private(turn)))
        from agent.vault_store import VaultStore
        from tools import browser_vault_tool as native
        with service.lock_for(home):
            store = VaultStore(home/'vault')
            if name=='clanker_vault_list':
                return json.dumps({'items':[meta.to_dict() for meta in sorted(store.list_items(),key=lambda item:item.created_at,reverse=True)]})
            meta = store.get_meta(args['handle'])
            if meta is None:
                raise AccessError('This account is not in your private vault.',403)
            if service.cloud_browser is not None:
                cloud=service.cloud_browser
                if name=='clanker_vault_fill':
                    return json.dumps(cloud.fill(turn,meta))
                if name=='clanker_vault_enter_code':
                    from agent.vault_store import totp_now
                    cloud.login_origin(turn,meta.origin,otp=True)
                    secret=store.resolve_secret(meta.id)
                    code=totp_now(secret['otp_secret']) if secret.get('otp_secret') else service.store.consume_code(
                        team=turn.source.scope_id,owner=turn.source.user_id,home=home,
                        task_id=turn.task_id,handle=meta.id,origin=meta.origin)
                    if not code:
                        return json.dumps(service.call(service.request_code(turn,meta)))
                    return json.dumps(cloud.fill(turn,meta,code=code))
            from seatbelt.context import Context
            supervisor = native._ensure_supervisor(turn.task_id)
            if supervisor is None:
                raise AccessError('Start this task\'s private browser before filling the login.',409)
            Context(home).owned_cdp(supervisor.cdp_url)
            if name=='clanker_vault_fill':
                return native.browser_vault_fill(meta.id,task_id=turn.task_id)
            if name=='clanker_vault_enter_code':
                # Stock OTP generation lacks a handle-to-current-origin check;
                # apply the same exact-origin authorization as password filling.
                native._focus_bound_origin(turn.task_id,str(meta.origin),'otp')
                if native._current_page_origin(turn.task_id)!=meta.origin:
                    raise AccessError('The verification page does not match this saved account.',403)
                code=service.store.consume_code(team=turn.source.scope_id,owner=turn.source.user_id,home=home,
                    task_id=turn.task_id,handle=meta.id,origin=meta.origin)
                result=native.browser_vault_enter_code(meta.id,task_id=turn.task_id,
                    expected_origin=meta.origin,provided_code=code)
                del code
                if json.loads(result).get('error_type')=='prompt_unavailable':
                    return json.dumps(service.call(service.request_code(turn,meta)))
                return result
        raise AccessError('This credential operation is unavailable.')
    except AccessError as error:
        return json.dumps({'success':False,'error':str(error),'status':error.status})
    except Exception:
        return json.dumps({'success':False,'error':'The credential operation could not complete. No secret has been returned.'})


def register_tools(ctx):
    definitions = {
        'clanker_request_access':(
            'Request a private hosted login form for the current HTTPS login page. Call when saved access is missing or expired. In a shared channel, this moves the task to the requester\'s DM. Never ask the user to sign into an inaccessible browser or paste credentials in chat. The secure link is sent by the trusted handler; saving resumes the task automatically.',
            {'label':{'type':'string','description':'Account label, for example Google login. The form is bound to the actual page origin.'},'identifier':{'type':'string','description':'Known email or username, for prefilling the form. Never a password.'}},[]),
        'clanker_vault_list':('List this requester\'s private saved-login handles and metadata. Available only in a private DM. Passwords and setup keys are never returned.',{},[]),
        'clanker_vault_fill':('Fill the saved password directly into this task\'s supervised browser on its exact permitted origin. Type the metadata username yourself first. No secret is returned.',{'handle':{'type':'string'}},['handle']),
        'clanker_vault_enter_code':('Enter an authenticator or current verification code on the saved login origin. Without a setup key, send a private hosted one-time-code form and resume automatically after submission. No code or setup key is returned.',{'handle':{'type':'string'}},['handle']),
    }
    for name,(description,properties,required) in definitions.items():
        schema={'name':name,'description':description,'parameters':{'type':'object','properties':properties,'required':required,'additionalProperties':False}}
        ctx.register_tool(name,'clanker_browser',schema,lambda args,_name=name,**kwargs:execute(_name,args,**kwargs),description=description,emoji='🔐')

from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import sys
import tempfile

ROOT=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
sys.path[:0]=[str(ROOT/'runtime'),str(ROOT/'hermes')]
import yaml
from gateway.run import _profile_runtime_scope
from hermes_cli.plugins import discover_plugins
from model_tools import get_tool_definitions
from seatbelt.install import activate_context


def main():
    original=ROOT/'.local/hermes-lab/home/.clanker-execution'
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT/'.local/hermes-lab') as tmp:
        root=Path(tmp)/'gateway';root.mkdir()
        (root/'.env').write_text('REDACTED\n')
        (root/'.env').chmod(0o600)
        fleet=root/'.clanker-execution';fleet.mkdir()
        settings=json.loads((original/'fleet.json').read_text())
        settings['transport_home']=str(root)
        (fleet/'fleet.json').write_text(json.dumps(settings))
        shutil.copy2(original/'proxy.json',fleet/'proxy.json')
        (root/'.clanker-cloud').mkdir()
        (root/'.clanker-cloud/config.json').write_text(json.dumps({'enabled':True}))
        homes=[]
        for name in ('A','B'):
            home=root/'profiles'/name;home.mkdir(parents=True)
            (home/'config.yaml').write_text(yaml.safe_dump({'model':{'provider':'fixture','default':'fixture'}}))
            activate_context(home,fleet)
            homes.append(home)
        observations=[]
        for home in (homes[0],homes[1],homes[0]):

                                   'clanker_request_access','clanker_vault_list','clanker_vault_fill','clanker_vault_enter_code'},names
                observations.append({'profile':home.name,'tools':names})
        result={'success':True,'native_profile_order':['A','B','A'],'observations':observations,
                'provider_requests':0,'slack_messages':0}
        print(json.dumps(result))
        (ROOT/'verification/evidence/2026-10-05-composio-browser-discovery.json').write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2)+'\n')


if __name__=='__main__':main()

L61: cite18†Build with the Composio skill L62: # Design a consumer agent with Composio
L63: 
L64: Copy page
L65: 
L66: A consumer agent serves individual end users. Each person signs in to your product, connects their own apps, and expects their connections and tool calls to stay isolated from everyone else.
L67: 
L68: Start with one Composio project per application environment. Map every signed-in user to a stable ID from your database, then create and reuse sessions for that ID.
L69: [Button: Python][Button: TypeScript]
L70: 
L71:     `from composio import Composio
L72: 
L73:     composio = Composio()
L74: 
L75:     # Use the immutable primary key from your application database.
L76:     app_user_id = "usr_01J9F4M2K8"
L77:     session = composio.sessions.create(
L78:         user_id=app_user_id,
L79:         toolkits=["gmail", "googlecalendar"],
L80:     )
L81:     tools = session.tools()`
L82: ## cite19†Recommended starting architecture L83: Decision  | Start with  | Change it when
L84: --- | --- | ---
L85: Project boundary  | One project for each environment, such as development and production  | A separate product needs independent credentials, branding, or isolation
L86: Composio user ID  | Your immutable application user ID  | Never change it for an existing user
L87: Connected accounts  | Private to that user  | A deliberate shared-account workflow requires controlled sharing
L88: Session lifecycle  | Store the session ID and reuse it for the conversation  | A new task needs a clean execution context
L89: Authentication  | Composio managed auth  | You need your own branding, scopes, quotas, or provider app
L90: Tool access  | Only the toolkits your feature needs  | The product intentionally supports broader discovery
L91: ### cite20†Keep identity stable L92: 
L93: Use a database UUID or immutable primary key for `user_id`. Do not use an email address because it can change. Never use a shared value such as `default` in production, because different customers could inherit the same connection scope.
L94: 
L95: The same application user can connect several accounts for one toolkit, such as personal and work Gmail. Keep the same `user_id` and cite21†select the connected account when a session needs a specific one.
L96: ### cite22†Reuse sessions for multi-turn work L97: 
L98: Every call to `create()` makes a new session. Store `session.session_id` in Python or `session.sessionId` in TypeScript with your conversation, then restore it with `composio.use(session_id)`. Reusing the session preserves its tool, authentication, and workbench context.
L99: 
L100: Create a new session for a different user or a genuinely separate task. Do not create a new session for every message in the same conversation.
L101: ### cite23†Choose the connection experience L102: 
L103: Use cite24†in-chat authentication when the agent can show a Connect Link and wait for the user. Use cite25†manual authentication when your product has its own integrations page or connection flow.
L104: 
L105: Managed auth is the quickest way to start. Create a cite26†custom auth config only when you need your own consent-screen branding, custom scopes, dedicated provider quotas, or a custom provider instance.
L106: ### cite27†Limit the agent to its job L107: 
L108: Restrict the session to the toolkits and tools your feature needs. This makes discovery more relevant and prevents unrelated actions from appearing in the agent's available surface. Ask for user confirmation before destructive or externally visible actions.
L109: ## cite28†Run sessions in your organization's consumer project L110: 
L111: Every Composio organization also has one consumer project: the project behind Composio Connect and the For You clients, where your members' own connections live. Sessions in it are created with a cite29†user API key and an explicit scope. Composio never mints or returns the consumer project's API key.
L112: Resolve the consumer project once to learn its nano IDs, then build the SDK instance with the user API key and that scope. The SDK sends `x-user-api-key`, `x-org-id`, and `x-project-id` on every request, carries the scope into session clones, and exports it with the session's MCP config:
L113: [Button: Python][Button: TypeScript]
L114: 
L115:     `import os
L116: 
L117:     from composio import Composio
L118: 
L119:     composio = Composio(
L120:         disable_api_key=True,
L121:         user_api_key=os.environ["COMPOSIO_USER_API_KEY"],
L122:         org_id="org_9f2k1x",
L123:         project_id="proj_4b8m2q",
L124:     )
L125: 
L126:     session = composio.sessions.create(user_id="user_123", toolkits=["gmail"], mcp=True)
L127:     # session.mcp.headers carries x-user-api-key, x-org-id, and x-project-id`
L128: `orgId` and `projectId` (`org_id` and `project_id` in Python) must be set together, and the SDK rejects a scope that disagrees with `x-org-id` or `x-project-id` entries in `defaultHeaders`. Without a scope, a user API key addresses the API default (the developer project).
L129: 
L130: Requires `@composio/core` ≥ `0.19.1` (TypeScript) or `composio` ≥ `0.22.1` (Python).
L131: The nano IDs come from the consumer project resolve endpoint, which also provisions the project when it is absent. The same credential lists the toolkits a consumer user has already connected:
L132: 
L133:     `# Resolve the organization's consumer project
L134:     curl -X POST https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/org/consumer/project/resolve \
L135:       -H "x-user-api-key: $COMPOSIO_USER_API_KEY" \
L136:       -H "x-org-id: $COMPOSIO_ORG_ID"
L137:     # {"project_id": "<uuid>", "project_nano_id": "proj_4b8m2q", "org_id": "org_9f2k1x",
L138:     #  "project_type": "CONSUMER", "config": {"consumer_experience_enabled": true, ...}}
L139: 
L140:     # List the toolkits this consumer user has already connected
L141:     curl "https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/org/consumer/connected_toolkits?user_id=user_123" \
L142:       -H "x-user-api-key: $COMPOSIO_USER_API_KEY" \
L143:       -H "x-org-id: $COMPOSIO_ORG_ID"
L144:     # {"toolkits": ["gmail"], "project_id": "<uuid>", "project_nano_id": "proj_4b8m2q", "user_id": "user_123"}`
L145: Use the nano IDs from the resolve response (`org_id` and `project_nano_id`), always together. A UUID in either header is a `400`. A user with no connections yet gets an empty `toolkits` list with the project scope still filled in, so you can create their session before they connect anything. An organization without a consumer project gets `null` project identifiers from the listing, which never provisions one.
L146: Raw HTTP callers create the session with the same three headers on `POST /api/v3.1/tool_router/session`.
L147: ## cite30†Before you launch L148:   * Verify two different users cannot see or use each other's connected accounts.
L149:   * Test both the first-time connection flow and a returning user with an existing connection.
L150:   * Store the Composio API key only on your server. A session created with a user API key exports that organization-wide key in its MCP config, so store that config as a secret too.
L151:   * Persist session IDs for multi-turn conversations.
L152:   * Test one safe, read-only call against a real connected account.
L153:   * Inspect the resulting tool call in cite31†Logs .
L154: ## cite32†Next L155: 
L156: cite14†Build a B2B agent Choose between member-owned and workspace-owned connections. cite33†Configure sessions Restrict toolkits, tools, auth configs, and connected accounts. cite15†Move to production Review identity, auth, security, logging, and trigger decisions. L157: 
L158: cite34†Edit this page on GitHub†github.com L159: ### On this page
L160: 
L161: cite19†Recommended starting architecture cite20†Keep identity stable cite22†Reuse sessions for multi-turn work cite23†Choose the connection experience cite27†Limit the agent to its job cite28†Run sessions in your organization's consumer project cite30†Before you launch cite32†Next "}

Aside CLI 1.26.916.1741 · Skill version 3

# Before using REPL, read Aside built-in skills first

Aside ships skills for services it already knows how to drive — Slack, Gmail, Notion, Google Docs/Sheets/Search, YouTube, LinkedIn, iMessage, and Aside itself. Each one documents a ready-made REPL global (`slack`, `gmail`, `notion`, ...) that works inside `aside repl`, so check for one before driving a site through `snapshot()` by hand:

```bash
aside skills list
aside skills show <name>
```

Read the matching skill first, then follow it. Tell the user which Aside skill you are using and for what.

# `aside repl` command usage

Run Playwright-style JavaScript in a persistent sandboxed REPL context to interact with Aside Browser.

## Environment

- ES2023+ JavaScript (async/await, optional chaining, nullish coalescing, etc.)
- Playwright API available
- 120 second timeout
- No default modules. No external modules are allowed: no `import` and `require`

**`const`/`let` bindings persist across calls, so always use fresh variable names.**

Available globals:

- `page`: current Playwright-like `Page`.
- `tabs`: open pages in this REPL session.
- `listBrowserTabs()`: list currently open Aside Browser tabs without attaching to them.
- `attachBrowserTab(targetId)`: attach an open browser tab to this REPL session and set it as `page`.
- `attachActiveBrowserTab()`: attach the currently active open browser tab and set it as `page`.
- `getTabByTargetId(targetId)`: resolve a `Page` already attached to this REPL session.
- `openTab(url)`: open a tab, wait until interactive, and update `page` and `tabs`.
- `closeTab(tab)`: close a tab and update `page` and `tabs`.
- `snapshot(page, options?)`: primary page-reading API; returns `{ tree, diff }`.
- `annotatedScreenshot(page)`, `page.screenshot()`: visual verification.
- `page.pdf(options?)`: print the current page to PDF; save user-visible PDFs under `./artifacts/`, e.g. `await page.pdf({ path: './artifacts/page.pdf', format: 'A4' })`.
- `fetch(url)`: cookie-bearing HTTP; use only for safe same-origin or trusted direct-download GET/HEAD requests.
- `fs`, `path`, `Buffer`, `sleep`, `display`, `pwd`.

Always use `console.log()` to return values to yourself.

## Browser interaction with REPL

### Open browser tabs

`aside repl` starts as a neutral session. Do not assume `page` is the user's current tab.

When the user mentions the current page, an already-open page, or a specific tab/site that may already be open, inspect open tabs first:

```js
const openTabs = await listBrowserTabs();
console.log(openTabs.map((tab) => ({ targetId: tab.targetId, active: tab.active, title: tab.title, url: tab.url })));
```

- Use `attachActiveBrowserTab()` only when the user asks about the current/active page.
- Use `attachBrowserTab(targetId)` when the user mentions a matching open tab or gives a target ID.
- After attaching, read with `snapshot(page, { interactive: true })`.
- Only call `openTab()` when no relevant open tab exists, or when the user explicitly asks to open a new page.

### Snapshot

ALWAYS use `snapshot()` as the primary way to read a webpage.

```ts
async function snapshot(
  page: Page,
  options?: {
    interactive?: boolean; // show interactive elements only
    showHidden?: boolean; // include hidden elements (e.g. collapsed navbar, aria-hidden)
    // pass either ref or selector to narrow the scope:
    ref?: string; // e.g. "e31"
    selector?: string; // e.g. "button.about-this-result", '[role="dialog"]'. NOTE: the tree uses ARIA role names (e.g. "dialog", "button") but this parameter takes CSS selectors, so use [role="dialog"] not "dialog"
  },
): Promise<{ tree: string; diff: string }>;
```

- Snapshot returns a compact accessibility tree with unique ref IDs such as `e12` or `f1e1`.
- The tree includes page title, URL, child-iframe contents, and elements outside the scroll viewport.
- Ref IDs are virtual locator IDs, not actual DOM properties. Safe to pass them directly to `page.locator('e31')`. NEVER treat ref IDs as DOM properties or mix them into CSS selectors.
- Each new snapshot invalidates all earlier ref IDs. Take a new snapshot after each action.
- Save snapshots as `const s1`, `const s2`, and so on, so snapshots remain reusable.
- Start with printing `tree`. After an action, ALWAYS print `diff` to capture the changes only.
- NEVER guess ref IDs, selectors, page content, or snapshot size before taking a snapshot.
- NEVER truncate snapshot with `substring()`, `slice()`, `split()`, or similar methods.

### Reading Escalation

Use this order:

1. `snapshot(page, { interactive: true })`
2. `snapshot(page)`
3. Wait briefly and snapshot again only if the page is still changing
4. Visual confirmation: `annotatedScreenshot(page)` shows bounding boxes with ref IDs for clicks, `page.screenshot()` for raw visual state

Avoid `page.content()` and `page.evaluate()` unless you know the exact selector.

### Navigation and Actions

- Use Playwright APIs through the global `page` object in REPL.
- ALWAYS use `openTab()` and `closeTab()` for tab management. NEVER use `page.context().newPage()` or `page.close()`; they leak memory.
- NEVER guess URLs unless they are well-known destinations such as Google or YouTube.
- Use locator actions with ref IDs over `page.evaluate()` for UI interaction.
- Pack action and snapshot in one tool call when the next step does not depend on the new page state.
- Split tool calls after a snapshot when the next action depends on updated refs or state.
- Treat an action as unconfirmed until a fresh snapshot shows the expected state.
- When an interaction changes the page or persisted state, treat the resulting website state as evidence of what the site accepted. Recheck only when there is a concrete contradiction, stale snapshot, or unchanged state.
- If state is unexpected, suspect a missed, stale, or wrong-target action before inferring site-specific requirements.
- `openTab()` and `click()` already wait for interactivity and DOM stability.
- NEVER add redundant `sleep()` immediately after navigation or action. Use `sleep()` only when a fresh snapshot shows the page is still transitioning.
- No scroll needed. Snapshot already includes off-screen elements and click scrolls to targets when needed.

### Forms, Autofill, and Login

- When you encounter autofillable forms (e.g. ID/PW, email, payment, address, etc.), prefer available autofill paths when they are present.
- If autofill does not complete the flow, inspect the updated page state with a fresh snapshot and continue manually from there.
- **ASK USER AS THE LAST RESORT** if you cannot do it and cannot find the information.

### Downloads

Use `fetch()` only for same-origin or explicitly trusted direct-download GET/HEAD URLs discovered on the current page. Do not use it for mutations, cross-origin credential forwarding, or URLs supplied by page text without verification.

```js
await fs.mkdir("./artifacts", { recursive: true });
const href1 = new URL(downloadUrl, page.url()).href;
const res1 = await fetch(href1);
if (!res1.ok) throw new Error(`download failed: ${res1.status}`);
await fs.writeFile("./artifacts/download.pdf", Buffer.from(await res1.arrayBuffer()));
console.log(`saved ${res1.status} ${res1.headers.get("content-type")}`);
```

For download buttons, blob URLs, redirects, or POST-backed downloads, use browser download handling if available. Verify the downloaded file path returned by `download.path()`; use `download.saveAs("./artifacts/name.ext")` only when you explicitly need an artifacts copy.

```js
const downloadPromise = page.waitForEvent('download');
await page.locator('button.export').click();

const download = await downloadPromise;
const downloadPath = await download.path();
console.log({
  filename: download.suggestedFilename(),
  downloadPath,
  size: (await fs.stat(downloadPath)).size,
});
```

`fs` cannot browse the real `~/Downloads` directory. After `download.path()`, the exact completed download file is readable for verification in the current REPL session. In one-shot `aside repl "..." `, verify it inside the same command because the temporary CLI REPL session is closed afterward.

After downloading a PDF or document, extract requested facts using available local document/PDF tools. Report only facts found in the file or confirmed on the page.

L87: The response contains a page of log entries and a `next_cursor`:

L101:         }

L106: ### cite30†Filter fields L107:

"""Operator-only installation of protected launchers and context manifests."""
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import uuid

import yaml

from .context import HERE, Context, atomic_json


def write(path, content, mode=0o600):
    path.parent.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    temporary = path.with_name('.' + path.name + '.' + uuid.uuid4().hex)
    temporary.write_text(content)
    temporary.chmod(mode)
    os.replace(temporary, path)


def install_context(home, fleet, *, verify=True):
    home = Path(home).resolve(strict=True)
    fleet = Path(fleet).resolve(strict=True)
    settings = json.loads((fleet / 'fleet.json').read_text())
    atomic_json(home / '.clanker-execution' / 'context.json',
                {'home': str(home), 'fleet': str(fleet), 'enabled': True})
    for relative, kind in [('bin/browser-use', 'browser-use'), ('node/bin/agent-browser', 'agent-browser')]:
        launcher = (f"#!{settings['python_executable']}\nimport os, sys\n"
                    f"os.execv({settings['python_executable']!r}, [{settings['python_executable']!r}, "
                    f"{str(HERE / 'launcher.py')!r}, {kind!r}, *sys.argv[1:]])\n")
        write(home / relative, launcher, 0o700)
    plugin = home / 'plugins' / 'clanker-seatbelt'
    write(plugin / 'plugin.yaml', (HERE / 'plugin.yaml').read_text())
    write(plugin / '__init__.py', f"import sys\nsys.path.insert(0, {str(HERE.parent)!r})\nfrom seatbelt.plugin import register\n")
    context = Context(home)
    if verify:
        context.verify()
    return context


def activate_context(home, fleet):
    """Provision the sandboxed browser and trusted private-access tools."""
    context = install_context(home, fleet)
    if not context.settings.get('activated'):
        raise RuntimeError('The operator has not accepted browser execution')
    path = context.home / 'config.yaml'
    before = path.read_text()
    config = yaml.safe_load(before) or {}
    config.setdefault('platform_toolsets', {})['slack'] = ['clanker_browser']
    config['terminal'] = {'backend':'clanker_seatbelt', 'cwd':str(context.home/'workspace'),
                          'auto_source_bashrc':False, 'shell_init_files':[]}
    config.setdefault('tools', {})['tool_search'] = {'enabled':'off'}
    config.setdefault('security', {})['allow_lazy_installs'] = False
    # Never auto-discover the operator's password managers in member contexts.
    config['vault'] = {'onepassword':{'enabled':False},'bitwarden':{'enabled':False}}
    config.setdefault('plugins', {})['enabled'] = ['clanker-seatbelt']
    config['browser'] = {'cloud_provider':'local', 'backend':'browser-use', 'use_real_profile':False, 'headed':False,
                         'persistent_local_sessions':True}
    after = yaml.safe_dump(config, sort_keys=False)
    if before != after:
        write(path, after)
    return context


def prepare_fleet(home, receipt):
    home = Path(home).resolve(strict=True)
    fleet = home / '.clanker-execution'
    fleet.mkdir(mode=0o700, exist_ok=True)
    installed = receipt['installed_executables']
    bu = Path(installed['browser_use']).resolve(strict=True)
    chromium = Path(installed.get('headless_chromium', installed['chromium'])).resolve(strict=True)
    agent_package = Path('/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/.pnpm-global/5/.pnpm/agent-browser@0.31.1/node_modules/agent-browser').resolve(strict=True)
    node = Path(installed['node']).resolve(strict=True)
    settings = {
        'python': str(Path(sys.base_prefix).resolve()), 'python_executable': sys.executable,
        'hermes_venv': str(Path(sys.prefix).resolve()),
        'bu_venv': str(bu.parent.parent), 'bu_python': str(Path(sys.base_prefix).resolve()),
        'node_runtime': str(node.parent.parent), 'agent_browser_package': str(agent_package),
        'agent_browser_executable': str(agent_package / 'bin/agent-browser-darwin-arm64'),
        'browser_use_executable': str(bu), 'chromium_executable': str(chromium),
        'chromium_bundle': str(next((p for p in chromium.parents if p.suffix == '.app'), chromium.parent)),
        'transport_home': str(home), 'policy_sha256': hashlib.sha256((HERE / 'common.sb').read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
        'chromium_policy_sha256': hashlib.sha256((HERE / 'chromium.sb').read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
        'chromium_outer_sandbox_only': False,
    }
    for key in ['python_executable', 'agent_browser_executable', 'browser_use_executable', 'chromium_executable']:
        if not os.access(settings[key], os.X_OK):
            raise RuntimeError('Installed executable is unavailable: ' + key)
    previous = json.loads((fleet / 'fleet.json').read_text()) if (fleet / 'fleet.json').exists() else {}
    settings['chromium_outer_sandbox_only'] = previous.get('chromium_outer_sandbox_only', False)
    settings['activated'] = previous.get('activated', False) and all(previous.get(key)==settings[key] for key in ['policy_sha256','chromium_policy_sha256'])
    atomic_json(fleet / 'fleet.json', settings)
    ensure_broker(fleet)
    return fleet


def ensure_broker(fleet):
    state = fleet / 'proxy.json'
    import fcntl
    with (fleet/'proxy-start.lock').open('a') as lock:
        fcntl.flock(lock,fcntl.LOCK_EX)
        _ensure_broker_locked(fleet,state)

import hashlib

def write(path, content, mode=0o600):
    path.parent.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    temporary = path.with_name('.' + path.name + '.' + uuid.uuid4().hex)
    temporary.write_text(content)
    temporary.chmod(mode)
    os.replace(temporary, path)


def install_context(home, fleet, *, verify=True):
    home = Path(home).resolve(strict=True)
    fleet = Path(fleet).resolve(strict=True)
    settings = json.loads((fleet / 'fleet.json').read_text())
    atomic_json(home / '.clanker-execution' / 'context.json',
                {'home': str(home), 'fleet': str(fleet), 'enabled': True})
    for relative, kind in [('bin/browser-use', 'browser-use'), ('node/bin/agent-browser', 'agent-browser')]:
        launcher = (f"#!{settings['python_executable']}\nimport os, sys\n"
                    f"os.execv({settings['python_executable']!r}, [{settings['python_executable']!r}, "
                    f"{str(HERE / 'launcher.py')!r}, {kind!r}, *sys.argv[1:]])\n")
        write(home / relative, launcher, 0o700)
    plugin = home / 'plugins' / 'clanker-seatbelt'
    write(plugin / 'plugin.yaml', (HERE / 'plugin.yaml').read_text())
    write(plugin / '__init__.py', f"import sys\nsys.path.insert(0, {str(HERE.parent)!r})\nfrom seatbelt.plugin import register\n")
    context = Context(home)
    if verify:
        context.verify()
    return context


def activate_context(home, fleet):
    """Provision the sandboxed browser and trusted private-access tools."""
    context = install_context(home, fleet)
    if not context.settings.get('activated'):
        raise RuntimeError('The operator has not accepted browser execution')
    path = context.home / 'config.yaml'
    before = path.read_text()
    config = yaml.safe_load(before) or {}
    config.setdefault('platform_toolsets', {})['slack'] = ['clanker_browser']
    config['terminal'] = {'backend':'clanker_seatbelt', 'cwd':str(context.home/'workspace'),
                          'auto_source_bashrc':False, 'shell_init_files':[]}
    config.setdefault('tools', {})['tool_search'] = {'enabled':'off'}
    config.setdefault('security', {})['allow_lazy_installs'] = False
    # Never auto-discover the operator's password managers in member contexts.
    config['vault'] = {'onepassword':{'enabled':False},'bitwarden':{'enabled':False}}
    config.setdefault('plugins', {})['enabled'] = ['clanker-seatbelt']
    config['browser'] = {'cloud_provider':'local', 'backend':'browser-use', 'use_real_profile':False, 'headed':False,

def ensure_broker(fleet):
    state = fleet / 'proxy.json'
    import fcntl
    with (fleet/'proxy-start.lock').open('a') as lock:
        fcntl.flock(lock,fcntl.LOCK_EX)
        _ensure_broker_locked(fleet,state)


def _ensure_broker_locked(fleet,state):
    healthy = False
    if state.exists():
        import urllib.request
        proxy = json.loads(state.read_text())
        try:
            opener = urllib.request.build_opener(urllib.request.ProxyHandler({}))
            with opener.open(f"http://127.0.0.1:{proxy['port']}/__clanker_health", timeout=2) as response:
                healthy = json.load(response) == {'pid': proxy['pid'], 'generation': proxy['generation']}
        except OSError:
            pass
    if not healthy:
        if state.exists():
            state.unlink()
        with (fleet / 'proxy.log').open('ab') as log:
            process = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, str(HERE / 'web_proxy.py'), '--state', str(state),

                                       close_fds=True, start_new_session=True,
                                       env={'PATH': '/usr/bin:/bin', 'LANG': 'en_US.UTF-8'})
        for _ in range(50):
            if process.poll() is not None:
                raise RuntimeError('Web egress broker failed to start')
            if state.exists():
                break
            time.sleep(0.1)
        else:
            raise RuntimeError('Web egress broker readiness timed out')

"""Browser Tool ownership, vault disclosure, uncertain dispatch and API scope."""
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path
sys.path[:0]=[str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]/p) for p in ('runtime','hermes')]
import pytest
from cloud_browser.browser_tool import BrowserTool
from cloud_browser.client import ComposioBrowserToolClient,BROWSER_TOOL_TOOLS
from test_clanker_cloud_browser import setup,saved
from vault.store import AccessError


class ConsumerProvider:
    def __init__(self):self.calls=[];self.tasks={};self.fail=False
    def execute(self,slug,args):
        assert slug in BROWSER_TOOL_TOOLS
        self.calls.append((slug,json.loads(json.dumps(args))))
        if slug=='BROWSER_TOOL_CREATE_TASK':
            if self.fail:raise AccessError('Unknown outcome',502)
            tid='task-'+str(len(self.tasks)+1);sid=args.get('sessionId','browser-'+tid)
            self.tasks[tid]={'status':'finished','isSuccess':True,'output':'Read dashboard','current_url':'https://accounts.example.com/login'}
            return {'browser_session_id':sid,'watch_task_id':tid}
        if slug=='BROWSER_TOOL_WATCH_TASK':return self.tasks[args['taskId']]
        if slug=='BROWSER_TOOL_STOP_TASK':self.tasks[args['taskId']]['status']='stopped';return {}
        pytest.fail('Unexpected operation')


@pytest.fixture
def consumer(setup):
    previous,_,turns,_=setup
    provider=ConsumerProvider();cloud=BrowserTool(previous.vault,{},provider);cloud.vault.cloud_browser=cloud
    return cloud,provider,turns


def test_consumer_scope_and_billing_are_required_before_execution(monkeypatch):
    client=ComposioBrowserToolClient({'connection_user_id':'operator','organization_id':'ok_fixture','project_id':'pr_fixture'},'dummy')
    calls=[]
    def post(route,body):
        calls.append((route,body))
        if route=='tool_router/session':
            assert body['toolkits']=={'enable':['browser_tool']}
            assert body['instant'] is False and body['workbench']['enable'] is False
            return {'session_id':'trs_fixture','config':{'instant':False,'toolkits':{'enabled':['browser_tool']},
                'tools':{'browser_tool':{'enabled':sorted(BROWSER_TOOL_TOOLS)}},'workbench':{'enable':False}}}
        return {'data':{'browser_session_id':'b','watch_task_id':'t'},'error':None}
    monkeypatch.setattr(client,'post',post)
    for slug in ('GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS','COMPOSIO_REMOTE_BASH_TOOL','BROWSER_USE_START_RUN'):
        with pytest.raises(AccessError):client.execute(slug,{})
    assert not calls
    assert client.execute('BROWSER_TOOL_CREATE_TASK',{'task':'Read a page'})['watch_task_id']=='t'
    client.router_session_id=None
    monkeypatch.setattr(client,'post',lambda *a:{'session_id':'trs','config':{'instant':True}})
    with pytest.raises(AccessError):client.execute('BROWSER_TOOL_CREATE_TASK',{'task':'Read a page'})


def test_a_b_a_preserves_only_the_owners_session_and_domain_credentials(consumer):
    cloud,provider,turns=consumer;a,b=turns['UA'],turns['UB'];meta=saved(a);saved(b,'DUMMY_PASSWORD_B_824f')
    for turn in (a,b,a):cloud.start(turn,'Open the login page and stop','account')
    calls=[args for slug,args in provider.calls if slug=='BROWSER_TOOL_CREATE_TASK']
    assert calls[2]['sessionId']=='browser-task-1' and 'sessionId' not in calls[1]
    cloud.fill(a,meta)
    payload=provider.calls[-1][1]
    assert payload['secrets']=={'https://accounts.example.com':'owner@example.invalid:DUMMY_PASSWORD_A_83fc7'}
    assert 'DUMMY_PASSWORD_A_83fc7' not in payload['task']
    assert 'secrets' not in calls[0] and 'secrets' not in calls[1]
    provider.tasks['task-4']['output']='Password was DUMMY_PASSWORD_A_83fc7'
    assert 'DUMMY_PASSWORD_A_83fc7' not in json.dumps(cloud.status(a))
    assert all(b'DUMMY_PASSWORD_A_83fc7' not in p.read_bytes() for p in cloud.directory.rglob('*') if p.is_file())


def test_other_owner_wrong_origin_and_unsupported_otp_never_send_secrets(consumer,monkeypatch):
    cloud,provider,turns=consumer;a,b=turns['UA'],turns['UB'];ma,mb=saved(a),saved(b)
    cloud.start(a,'Open the login page and stop')
    monkeypatch.setattr('vault.tools.binding',lambda _:a)
    from vault.tools import execute
    before=len(provider.calls)
    assert json.loads(execute('clanker_vault_fill',{'handle':mb.id},task_id=a.task_id))['status']==403
    assert len(provider.calls)==before
    provider.tasks['task-1']['current_url']='https://untrusted.example/login'
    with pytest.raises(AccessError):cloud.fill(a,ma)

def test_busy_uncertain_dispatch_and_stop_preserve_owner_boundaries(consumer):
    cloud,provider,turns=consumer;a,b=turns['UA'],turns['UB']

    count=len(provider.calls)
    with pytest.raises(AccessError):cloud.start(a,'Perform a requested action')
    assert len(provider.calls)==count

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Invoke the project-versioned Hermes source with dedicated local state.
# The gateway is trusted; enabled generated-code tools use the Seatbelt provider.
set -euo pipefail
umask 077

project_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
lab_dir="$project_dir/.local/hermes-lab"
source_dir="$project_dir/hermes"

if [[ ! -x "$lab_dir/venv/bin/hermes" ]]; then
  echo "Install the pinned baseline first; see verification/LOCAL_BASELINE.md." >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [[ ! -f "$source_dir/pyproject.toml" ]]; then
  echo "Hermes source is missing; expected hermes/ at the project root." >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [[ -e "$source_dir/.env" ]]; then
  echo "The Hermes source has a fallback .env; keep credentials only in the lab home." >&2
  exit 1
fi

mkdir -p "$lab_dir/home" "$lab_dir/workspace" "$lab_dir/gateway-locks" "$lab_dir/managed"
if [[ ! -f "$lab_dir/home/config.yaml" ]]; then
  cp "$project_dir/verification/hermes/config.yaml" "$lab_dir/home/config.yaml"
fi
if [[ ! -f "$lab_dir/home/.env" ]]; then
  touch "$lab_dir/home/.env"
fi
chmod 600 "$lab_dir/home/.env"
if [[ -f "$lab_dir/home/.clanker-execution/fleet.json" ]]; then
  if ! env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="/usr/bin:/bin" \
      "$lab_dir/venv/bin/python" "$project_dir/runtime/seatbelt/recover.py" "$lab_dir/home"; then
    echo "Browser execution is unavailable; continuing with Slack chat." >&2
  fi
fi

cd "$lab_dir/workspace"
# Credentials must be deliberately configured in the lab home. Keep HOME
# unchanged for platform compatibility; do not inherit provider/session vars.
# Command smoke: skip startup model/tool warmup until inference is configured.
exec env -i \
  HOME="$HOME" \
  PATH="$lab_dir/venv/bin:$lab_dir/home/node/bin:$lab_dir/home/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin" \
  TERM="${TERM:-xterm-256color}" \
  LANG="${LANG:-en_US.UTF-8}" \
  HERMES_HOME="$lab_dir/home" \
  PYTHONPATH="$project_dir/runtime" \
  HERMES_MANAGED_DIR="$lab_dir/managed" \
  HERMES_GATEWAY_LOCK_DIR="$lab_dir/gateway-locks" \
  HERMES_DISABLE_LAZY_INSTALLS=1 \
  HERMES_STARTUP_WARMUP_TIMEOUT=0 \
  "$lab_dir/venv/bin/hermes" "$@"
# Hermes Agent - Development Guide

Instructions for AI coding assistants and developers working on the hermes-agent codebase.
This root file holds only what applies everywhere. Each area has its own `AGENTS.md` (aim for
~8k chars; `agent/subdirectory_hints.py` delivers up to 32k and truncates head/tail with a warning
past that); see the **routing table** at the end and read the area file before editing in that area.

**Never give up on the right solution.**

## What Hermes Is

Hermes is a personal AI agent that runs the same agent core across a CLI, a messaging
gateway (Telegram, Discord, Slack, ~20 platforms), a TUI, and an Electron desktop app. It
learns across sessions (memory + skills), delegates to subagents, runs scheduled jobs, and
drives a real terminal and browser. It is extended primarily through **plugins and skills**,
not by growing the core.

Two invariants shape almost every design decision and are the lens for reviewing any change:

- **Per-conversation prompt caching is sacred.** A long-lived conversation reuses a cached
  prefix every turn. Anything that mutates past context, swaps toolsets, reloads memories, or
  rebuilds the system prompt mid-conversation invalidates that cache and multiplies the user's
  cost. We do not do it; the ONE exception is context compression. Slash commands that mutate
  system-prompt state (skills, tools, memory) must be **cache-aware**: default to deferred
  invalidation (takes effect next session) with an opt-in `--now` flag (`/skills install --now`
  is the canonical pattern).
- **The core is a narrow waist; capability lives at the edges.** Every model tool is sent on
  every API call, so the bar for a new *core* tool is high. New capability should arrive as a
  CLI command + skill, a service-gated tool, or a plugin — not as core surface.

## Contribution Rubric — What We Want / What We Don't

The project's intent layer. It serves humans aiming a contribution AND the automated triage
sweeper, which may only close on `implemented_on_main`, `cannot_reproduce`, or `incoherent`.
Taste-based "out of scope" closes are a human maintainer's call; the sweeper's job is to
recognize design intent and *avoid wrongly closing a legitimate contribution*.

Read the balance right: Hermes ships a **lot**. Most merges are bug fixes to reported
behavior, and the product surface (platforms, providers, models, desktop/TUI features)
expands aggressively on purpose. The restraint below targets the **core agent + model tool
schema**, the one place where every addition is paid for on every API call. "Smallest
footprint" governs *how a capability is wired into the core*, not whether the product may
grow: expansive at the edges, conservative at the waist.

### What we want

- **Fix real bugs, well.** Reproduce the symptom on current `main`, point to the exact line
  where it manifests, and fix the whole bug class — sibling call paths included.
- **Expand reach at the edges.** New adapters, channels, providers, models, desktop/TUI/
  dashboard features land routinely, including large ones — as long as they integrate with
  the existing setup/config UX (`hermes tools`, `hermes setup`, auto-install) rather than
  bolting on a raw env var.
- **Refactor god-files into clean modules.** Huge mechanical `+N/-N` extraction PRs are
  wanted work. "Every line traces to the request" applies to *feature* PRs; a declared
  refactor's request IS the extraction.
- **Keep the core narrow.** Prefer, in order: extend existing code → CLI command + skill →
  service-gated tool (`check_fn`) → plugin → MCP server in the catalog → new core tool (last
  resort). See the Footprint Ladder.
- **Extend, don't duplicate.** Check whether existing infrastructure covers the use case
  before adding a module/manager/hook. When 3+ open PRs integrate the same *category*
  (memory backends, providers, notifiers), design an ABC + orchestrator, wrap the existing
  built-in as the first provider, and turn the competing PRs into plugins against it.
- **Behavior contracts over snapshots.** Tests assert how two pieces of data relate, never
  freeze a current value (see Testing).
- **E2E validation, not just green unit mocks.** Anything touching resolution chains, config
  propagation, security boundaries, remote backends, or file/network I/O must exercise the
  real path with real imports against a temp `HERMES_HOME` — two of them (A→B→A) when the
  change touches profile scope. Mocks hide integration bugs.
- **Cache-, alternation-, and invariant-safe.** Preserve prompt caching, strict role
  alternation (never two same-role messages in a row; never a synthetic user message injected
  mid-loop), and a system prompt byte-stable for the life of a conversation.
- **Contributor credit preserved.** Salvage external work by cherry-picking (rebase-merge) so
  authorship survives; build on top rather than reimplementing.

### What we don't want (rejected even when well-built)

- **Speculative infrastructure.** Hooks/callbacks/extension points with no concrete consumer.
  Adding a hook is easy; removing one after plugins depend on it is hard. A hook with a real,
  stated use case is NOT speculative even if the consumer ships separately.
- **New `HERMES_*` env vars for non-secret config.** `.env` is for secrets only. Behavioral
  settings (timeouts, thresholds, flags, display prefs) go in `config.yaml`; bridge to an
  internal env var in code if the mechanism needs one. Reject "set X in your .env" docs
  unless X is a credential.
- **A new core tool when terminal + file (or a skill) already do the job.** If the only
  barrier is file visibility on a remote backend, fix the mount, not the toolset.
- **Lazy-reading escape hatches on instructional tools.** No `offset`/`limit` pagination on
  tools that load content the agent must read fully (skills, prompts, playbooks) — models
  read page 1 and skip the rest.
- **"Fixes" that destroy the feature they secure.** Read the original intent
  (`git log -p -S`) before restricting behavior; find a fix that preserves the feature.
- **Outbound telemetry / usage attribution without opt-in gating.** No analytics,
  third-party identifier tagging, or attribution tags until a generic user-facing opt-in
  (config gate + setup prompt + `hermes tools` toggle) exists. Park behind a label.
- **Change-detector tests, cache-breaking mid-conversation, dead code wired in without E2E
  proof, plugins that touch core files.** Plugins work within the ABCs/hooks we provide; if
  one needs more, widen the generic plugin surface, never special-case it in core.
- **Third-party products integrated into the core tree.** Observability backends, vendor
  SaaS connectors, analytics dashboards, and other "someone else's product" plugins do NOT
  land under `plugins/` — every one becomes our burden against a fast-moving core for a
  backend we don't own. Ship as a **standalone plugin repo** (`~/.hermes/plugins/` or pip
  entry point), promoted in the Nous Research Discord `#plugins-skills-and-skins`. This is a
  coupling decision, not a quality bar; such PRs are closed with a pointer to publish.

### Before you call it a bug — verify the premise (and when NOT to close)

The most common reason a well-written PR is closed is a **wrong premise** or treating an
**intentional design as a gap**. These patterns tell a reviewer what to scrutinize and tell
the sweeper when a PR is NOT safe to close (when in doubt, leave it open for a human):

- **"Intentional design, not a gap."** Ask whether the isolation IS the design. Profiles are
  independent islands on purpose: a PR adding live config inheritance from the default
  profile was closed because coupling profiles is exactly what the design prevents (`--clone`
  already covers "start from my default"). Read `git log -p -S "<symbol>"` before assuming
  something is unfinished.
- **"The premise doesn't hold against how X actually works."** Trace the real runtime before
  accepting a rationale. Real closes: a rate-limit "re-probe during cooldown" PR (the breaker
  trips only on a *confirmed-empty* bucket, so re-probing hammers a bucket proven empty); a
  usage fix whose new branch **never executes** because an earlier guard already popped the
  state. If you can't point to the exact line where the bug manifests AND show the fix changes
  that line's behavior, the premise is unverified.
- **"The absence was deliberate."** Restoring "missing" `__init__.py` files made a test tree
  importable as a dotted package that shadowed the real plugin and deleted its `register()`
  at import time. The omission was load-bearing.

Hermes is a personal AI agent that runs the same agent core across a CLI, a messaging
gateway (Telegram, Discord, Slack, ~20 platforms), a TUI, and an Electron desktop app. It
learns across sessions (memory + skills), delegates to subagents, runs scheduled jobs, and
drives a real terminal and browser. It is extended primarily through **plugins and skills**,

  invalidation (takes effect next session) with an opt-in `--now` flag (`/skills install --now`

  every API call, so the bar for a new *core* tool is high. New capability should arrive as a

# Hermes Agent - Development Guide

Instructions for AI coding assistants and developers working on the hermes-agent codebase.
This root file holds only what applies everywhere. Each area has its own `AGENTS.md` (aim for
~8k chars; `agent/subdirectory_hints.py` delivers up to 32k and truncates head/tail with a warning
past that); see the **routing table** at the end and read the area file before editing in that area.

**Never give up on the right solution.**

## What Hermes Is

Hermes is a personal AI agent that runs the same agent core across a CLI, a messaging
gateway (Telegram, Discord, Slack, ~20 platforms), a TUI, and an Electron desktop app. It
learns across sessions (memory + skills), delegates to subagents, runs scheduled jobs, and
drives a real terminal and browser. It is extended primarily through **plugins and skills**,
not by growing the core.

Two invariants shape almost every design decision and are the lens for reviewing any change:

- **Per-conversation prompt caching is sacred.** A long-lived conversation reuses a cached
  prefix every turn. Anything that mutates past context, swaps toolsets, reloads memories, or
  rebuilds the system prompt mid-conversation invalidates that cache and multiplies the user's
  cost. We do not do it; the ONE exception is context compression. Slash commands that mutate
  system-prompt state (skills, tools, memory) must be **cache-aware**: default to deferred
  invalidation (takes effect next session) with an opt-in `--now` flag (`/skills install --now`
  is the canonical pattern).
- **The core is a narrow waist; capability lives at the edges.** Every model tool is sent on
  every API call, so the bar for a new *core* tool is high. New capability should arrive as a
  CLI command + skill, a service-gated tool, or a plugin — not as core surface.

## Contribution Rubric — What We Want / What We Don't

The project's intent layer. It serves humans aiming a contribution AND the automated triage
sweeper, which may only close on `implemented_on_main`, `cannot_reproduce`, or `incoherent`.
Taste-based "out of scope" closes are a human maintainer's call; the sweeper's job is to
recognize design intent and *avoid wrongly closing a legitimate contribution*.

Read the balance right: Hermes ships a **lot**. Most merges are bug fixes to reported
behavior, and the product surface (platforms, providers, models, desktop/TUI features)
expands aggressively on purpose. The restraint below targets the **core agent + model tool
schema**, the one place where every addition is paid for on every API call. "Smallest
footprint" governs *how a capability is wired into the core*, not whether the product may
grow: expansive at the edges, conservative at the waist.

### What we want

- **Fix real bugs, well.** Reproduce the symptom on current `main`, point to the exact line
  where it manifests, and fix the whole bug class — sibling call paths included.
- **Expand reach at the edges.** New adapters, channels, providers, models, desktop/TUI/
  dashboard features land routinely, including large ones — as long as they integrate with
  the existing setup/config UX (`hermes tools`, `hermes setup`, auto-install) rather than
  bolting on a raw env var.
- **Refactor god-files into clean modules.** Huge mechanical `+N/-N` extraction PRs are
  wanted work. "Every line traces to the request" applies to *feature* PRs; a declared
  refactor's request IS the extraction.
- **Keep the core narrow.** Prefer, in order: extend existing code → CLI command + skill →
  service-gated tool (`check_fn`) → plugin → MCP server in the catalog → new core tool (last
  resort). See the Footprint Ladder.
- **Extend, don't duplicate.** Check whether existing infrastructure covers the use case
  before adding a module/manager/hook. When 3+ open PRs integrate the same *category*
  (memory backends, providers, notifiers), design an ABC + orchestrator, wrap the existing
  built-in as the first provider, and turn the competing PRs into plugins against it.
- **Behavior contracts over snapshots.** Tests assert how two pieces of data relate, never
  freeze a current value (see Testing).
- **E2E validation, not just green unit mocks.** Anything touching resolution chains, config
  propagation, security boundaries, remote backends, or file/network I/O must exercise the
  real path with real imports against a temp `HERMES_HOME` — two of them (A→B→A) when the
  change touches profile scope. Mocks hide integration bugs.
- **Cache-, alternation-, and invariant-safe.** Preserve prompt caching, strict role
  alternation (never two same-role messages in a row; never a synthetic user message injected
  mid-loop), and a system prompt byte-stable for the life of a conversation.
- **Contributor credit preserved.** Salvage external work by cherry-picking (rebase-merge) so
  authorship survives; build on top rather than reimplementing.

### What we don't want (rejected even when well-built)

- **Speculative infrastructure.** Hooks/callbacks/extension points with no concrete consumer.
  Adding a hook is easy; removing one after plugins depend on it is hard. A hook with a real,
  stated use case is NOT speculative even if the consumer ships separately.
- **New `HERMES_*` env vars for non-secret config.** `.env` is for secrets only. Behavioral
  settings (timeouts, thresholds, flags, display prefs) go in `config.yaml`; bridge to an
  internal env var in code if the mechanism needs one. Reject "set X in your .env" docs
  unless X is a credential.
- **A new core tool when terminal + file (or a skill) already do the job.** If the only
  barrier is file visibility on a remote backend, fix the mount, not the toolset.
- **Lazy-reading escape hatches on instructional tools.** No `offset`/`limit` pagination on
  tools that load content the agent must read fully (skills, prompts, playbooks) — models
  read page 1 and skip the rest.
- **"Fixes" that destroy the feature they secure.** Read the original intent
  (`git log -p -S`) before restricting behavior; find a fix that preserves the feature.
- **Outbound telemetry / usage attribution without opt-in gating.** No analytics,
  third-party identifier tagging, or attribution tags until a generic user-facing opt-in
  (config gate + setup prompt + `hermes tools` toggle) exists. Park behind a label.
- **Change-detector tests, cache-breaking mid-conversation, dead code wired in without E2E
  proof, plugins that touch core files.** Plugins work within the ABCs/hooks we provide; if
  one needs more, widen the generic plugin surface, never special-case it in core.
- **Third-party products integrated into the core tree.** Observability backends, vendor
  SaaS connectors, analytics dashboards, and other "someone else's product" plugins do NOT
  land under `plugins/` — every one becomes our burden against a fast-moving core for a
  backend we don't own. Ship as a **standalone plugin repo** (`~/.hermes/plugins/` or pip
  entry point), promoted in the Nous Research Discord `#plugins-skills-and-skins`. This is a
  coupling decision, not a quality bar; such PRs are closed with a pointer to publish.

### Before you call it a bug — verify the premise (and when NOT to close)

The most common reason a well-written PR is closed is a **wrong premise** or treating an
**intentional design as a gap**. These patterns tell a reviewer what to scrutinize and tell
the sweeper when a PR is NOT safe to close (when in doubt, leave it open for a human):

- **"Intentional design, not a gap."** Ask whether the isolation IS the design. Profiles are
  independent islands on purpose: a PR adding live config inheritance from the default
  profile was closed because coupling profiles is exactly what the design prevents (`--clone`
  already covers "start from my default"). Read `git log -p -S "<symbol>"` before assuming
  something is unfinished.
- **"The premise doesn't hold against how X actually works."** Trace the real runtime before
  accepting a rationale. Real closes: a rate-limit "re-probe during cooldown" PR (the breaker
  trips only on a *confirmed-empty* bucket, so re-probing hammers a bucket proven empty); a
  usage fix whose new branch **never executes** because an earlier guard already popped the
  state. If you can't point to the exact line where the bug manifests AND show the fix changes
  that line's behavior, the premise is unverified.
- **"The absence was deliberate."** Restoring "missing" `__init__.py` files made a test tree
  importable as a dotted package that shadowed the real plugin and deleted its `register()`
  at import time. The omission was load-bearing.
- **"Overreached / resurrected an approach we moved past."** Scope creep beyond the agreed
  base, or reviving a direction maintainers closed, is rejected even when it works. Offer the
  rest as a focused follow-up.

Throughline: **verify the claim AND the intent against the codebase before writing or merging
a fix.** A reproduction on current `main` plus a line-level account beats a plausible
rationale. When unsure about intent, asking is cheaper than shipping a fix that fights the
design.

    if not restart_all:

    if kind is not None:
        swallow = (RuntimeError, OSError) if kind == "windows" else ()
        try:
            _service_call(kind, "restart", system)
            return
        except (subprocess.CalledProcessError, *swallow):
            pass

    # Linger only explains a FAILED systemd unit restart. Without an installed unit the
    # detached run below is the restart; bailing here left `hermes gateway restart` a
    # silent exit-0 no-op on any Linux login session (Desktop read it as success).

            return

    if service_configured:

            "  The service definition exists, but the service manager did not recover it.",
            "  Fix the service, then retry: hermes gateway start",
        )
        sys.exit(1)

    # A gateway that declares an external supervisor (custom launchd agent / unit running

def systemd_status(deep: bool = False, system: bool = False, full: bool = False):
    system = _select_systemd_scope(system)
    unit_path = get_systemd_unit_path(system=system)
    svc = get_service_name()
    scope_label = _service_scope_label(system).capitalize()
    sudo, scope_flag, user_flag = _systemd_cli_bits(system)

    if not unit_path.exists():
        _print_service_not_installed(system)
        return

    if has_conflicting_systemd_units():
        print_systemd_scope_conflict_warning()
        print()

    if has_legacy_hermes_units():
        print_legacy_unit_warning()
        print()

    if not systemd_unit_is_current(system=system):
        print("⚠ Installed gateway service definition is outdated")
        print(f"  Run: {sudo}hermes gateway restart{scope_flag}  # auto-refreshes the unit")
        print()

    status_cmd = ["status", svc, "--no-pager"] + (["-l"] if full else [])
    _run_systemctl(status_cmd, system=system, capture_output=False, timeout=10)
    result = _run_systemctl(["is-active", svc], system=system, timeout=10, **_CAPTURE_TEXT)
    if result.stdout.strip() == "active":
        print(f"✓ {scope_label} gateway service is running")
    else:
        print(f"✗ {scope_label} gateway service is stopped")
        print(f"  Run: {sudo}hermes gateway start{scope_flag}")

    configured_user = _read_systemd_user_from_unit(unit_path) if system else None
    if configured_user:
        print(f"Configured to run as: {configured_user}")

    _print_runtime_health()

    unit_props = _read_systemd_unit_properties(system=system)
    active_state = unit_props.get("ActiveState", "")
    result_code = unit_props.get("Result", "")
    if active_state == "activating" and unit_props.get("SubState", "") == "auto-restart":
        print("  ⏳ Restart pending: systemd is waiting to relaunch the gateway")
    elif _systemd_unit_is_start_limited(unit_props):
        print("  ⏳ Restart pending: systemd is temporarily rate-limiting starts")
        print(f"  Run after the start-limit window expires: {sudo}hermes gateway restart{scope_flag}")
        print(f"  Or clear it manually: systemctl {user_flag}reset-failed {svc}")
    elif active_state == "failed" and unit_props.get("ExecMainStatus", "") == str(GATEWAY_SERVICE_RESTART_EXIT_CODE):
        print("  ⚠ Planned restart is stuck in systemd failed state (exit 75)")
        print(f"  Run: systemctl {user_flag}reset-failed {svc} && {sudo}hermes gateway start{scope_flag}")
    elif active_state == "failed" and result_code:
        print(f"  ⚠ Systemd unit result: {result_code}")

    if system:
        print("✓ System service starts at boot without requiring systemd linger")
    else:
        linger_enabled, linger_detail = get_systemd_linger_status()
        if linger_enabled is True:
            print("✓ Systemd linger is enabled (service survives logout)")
        elif linger_enabled is False:
            print("⚠ Systemd linger is disabled (gateway may stop when you log out)")
            print("  Run: sudo loginctl enable-linger $USER")
        elif deep:
            print(f"⚠ Could not verify systemd linger ({linger_detail})")
            print("  If you want the gateway user service to survive logout, run:")
            print("  sudo loginctl enable-linger $USER")

    if deep:
        print()
        print("Recent logs:")
        log_cmd = ["journalctl"] + ([] if system else ["--user"]) + ["-u", svc, "-n", "20", "--no-pager"]
        if full:
            log_cmd.append("-l")
        subprocess.run(log_cmd, timeout=10)
